title: Build user preferences UI
description:
Create the settings/preferences UI and backend support.

## Scope

Based on TTRSS preferences audit (docs/ttrss-preferences-checklist.md):
- **22 configurable preferences** exposed in settings UI
- **7 hidden preferences** with sensible defaults (not in UI)
- **4 dropped** (single layout approach, no blacklisted tags)

## Settings Tabs Structure

1. **Feeds & Categories** — feed organizer (separate task ttrb-tdj)
2. **Reading** — display, behavior, sidebar prefs
3. **Appearance** — theme, custom CSS, language
4. **Digest** — email digest settings
5. **Account** — password, timezone, date formats

## Key UX Decisions

- Sorting controlled in list UI (persisted automatically), not settings
- Hide read feeds: quick toggle in sidebar + setting for default
- Responsive layout by default (no widescreen toggle)
- Categories always enabled

## Child Tasks

This epic has child tasks for each feature area:
- Purge/cleanup settings
- Feed update intervals
- Article display prefs
- Reading behavior prefs
- Feed sidebar controls
- Fresh article age
- Date/time formatting
- Theming system
- Search language
- Email digest settings
- Multi-column list sorting

## API

- GET /api/preferences — all user prefs
- PATCH /api/preferences — update prefs
- Backend: UserPreference model already exists
close_reason: Core user preferences UI is complete: UserPreference model, PreferencesController API, PreferencesContext provider, PreferencesPanel component, and SettingsDialog with tabs structure. Child tasks will add specific preference areas (theming, purge settings, sidebar controls, etc.).

title: Add responsive mobile layout
description:
# Responsive Mobile Layout Epic

Make the UI work well on mobile devices (phones and tablets).

## Decision Needed: Approach
**Open question from project owner**: Should this be implemented as:
1. **Responsive main UI** - Same React app, Tailwind responsive classes
2. **Separate mobile frontend** - Dedicated mobile-optimized React app
3. **Native mobile app** - React Native or similar for iOS/Android

The child tasks below assume Option 1 (responsive main UI) as it's the most pragmatic starting point. Can revisit if a separate mobile experience is desired.

## Current State
- Minimal responsive design (only dialog widths)
- Three-pane layout has fixed widths
- No touch gestures or mobile navigation
- Tailwind CSS already in use

## Goals
- Usable on phones (320px-480px width)
- Touch-friendly interactions
- Mobile navigation pattern (hamburger menu, slide-out sidebar)
- Efficient reading on small screens

## Child Tasks
See linked child issues for implementation details.

## Out of Scope (for now)
- Native mobile app
- PWA features (offline, install prompt)
- Push notifications

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Works on iPhone SE (375px width)
- [ ] Works on iPad (768px width)
- [ ] Sidebar collapses to hamburger menu on mobile
- [ ] Touch targets are at least 44px
- [ ] Swipe gestures for article navigation
- [ ] Pull-to-refresh on article list

## Overview
Implement a user-configurable accent color system that derives all theme colors from a single primary hue selection.

## Requirements

### Color Derivation (must be done in code, NOT hardcoded CSS)
1. User selects a primary accent hue (0-360) in Settings
2. JavaScript utility derives:
   - **Secondary color**: Complement of primary (hue + 180, wrapped at 360)
   - **Primary-light**: Higher lightness, slightly reduced saturation
   - **Primary-dark**: Lower lightness

title: Set up Guard for Rails auto-testing
description:
## Summary

Set up Guard with guard-minitest for automatic test running on file changes. This improves developer experience by providing instant feedback during development.

## Current State

- Rails 8.1.1 with Minitest (default test framework)
- No test directory exists yet
- No Guardfile configured

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Add gems to Gemfile (development group)

```ruby
group :development do
  gem "guard"
  gem "guard-minitest"
end
```

Run `bundle install`.

### 2. Initialize Guard

```bash
bundle exec guard init minitest
```

This generates a default Guardfile.

### 3. Configure Guardfile

Customize watch patterns for the app structure:

```ruby
guard :minitest, spring: false, all_on_start: false do
  watch(%r{^test/(.*)_test\.rb$})
  watch(%r{^lib/(.*/)?([^/]+)\.rb$})     { |m| "test/lib/#{m[1]}#{m[2]}_test.rb" }
  watch(%r{^test/test_helper\.rb$})      { "test" }

  # Rails specific
  watch(%r{^app/models/(.+)\.rb$})       { |m| "test/models/#{m[1]}_test.rb" }
  watch(%r{^app/controllers/(.+)\.rb$})  { |m| "test/controllers/#{m[1]}_test.rb" }
  watch(%r{^app/services/(.+)\.rb$})     { |m| "test/services/#{m[1]}_test.rb" }
  watch(%r{^app/jobs/(.+)\.rb$})         { |m| "test/jobs/#{m[1]}_test.rb" }
  watch(%r{^app/mailers/(.+)\.rb$})      { |m| "test/mailers/#{m[1]}_test.rb" }
end
```

### 4. Create test directory structure

```bash
mkdir -p test/{models,controllers,services,jobs,mailers,integration,system}
```

Create `test/test_helper.rb`:

```ruby
ENV["RAILS_ENV"] ||= "test"
require_relative "../config/environment"
require "rails/test_help"

class ActiveSupport::TestCase
  # Run tests in parallel with specified workers
  parallelize(workers: :number_of_processors)

  # Setup all fixtures in test/fixtures/*.yml
  fixtures :all
end
```

### 5. Usage

Start Guard in a terminal:

```bash
bundle exec guard
```

Guard will watch for file changes and automatically run corresponding tests.

## Optional Enhancements

- Add `guard-livereload` for browser refresh on asset changes
- Consider `minitest-reporters` for better test output formatting
- Add notification support (terminal-notifier on macOS)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Guard runs on `bundle exec guard`
- [ ] Saving a model file triggers its corresponding test
- [ ] Saving a controller file triggers its corresponding test
- [ ] Saving a service file triggers its corresponding test
- [ ] Test helper exists and works with `bin/rails test`
close_reason: Already implemented: Guardfile configured with watch patterns for models, controllers, services, jobs, mailers. guard-minitest gem in Gemfile. Run 'bundle exec guard' to start.

title: Set up Playwright E2E testing infrastructure
description:
## Summary

Configure Playwright for end-to-end testing of the React frontend. Playwright is already installed (`@playwright/test` in devDependencies) but needs configuration and initial test structure.

## Current State

- React 19 + TypeScript + shadcn/ui frontend (~2700 lines)

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Initialize Playwright config

```bash
npx playwright install
```

Create `playwright.config.ts`:

```typescript
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './e2e',
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,
  workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,
  reporter: 'html',
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
    },
    // Add firefox/webkit as needed
  ],
  webServer: {
    command: 'bin/rails server -p 3000',
    url: 'http://localhost:3000',
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
    timeout: 120 * 1000,
  },
});
```

### 2. Create test directory structure

```
e2e/
├── fixtures/
│   └── test-fixtures.ts    # Page objects, helpers
├── feed-management.spec.ts
├── article-reading.spec.ts
├── keyboard-navigation.spec.ts
└── auth.spec.ts
```

### 3. Add npm scripts to package.json

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test:e2e": "playwright test",
    "test:e2e:ui": "playwright test --ui",
    "test:e2e:debug": "playwright test --debug",
    "test:e2e:codegen": "playwright codegen http://localhost:3000"
  }
}
```

### 4. Create initial smoke test

```typescript
// e2e/smoke.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('app loads and shows feed sidebar', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
});
```

### 5. Create test fixtures/helpers

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/test-fixtures.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';

// Extend with app-specific fixtures
export const test = base.extend({
  // Add authenticated user fixture
  // Add seeded database fixture
});
```

### 6. Database seeding strategy

Options:
- Rails fixtures loaded via API endpoint (test-only)
- Factory-based seeding script
- Database snapshots

## Key Test Scenarios to Cover

1. **Authentication flow** - Login, logout, session persistence
2. **Feed management** - Subscribe, edit, unsubscribe, organize

4. **Keyboard navigation** - j/k navigation, shortcuts, command palette (Cmd+K)

## Usage

```bash

# Open UI mode (visual test runner)
```

title: Fix entry list scroll containment for keyboard navigation
description:
## Summary

When navigating entries with j/k keyboard shortcuts, the entire page scrolls instead of just the entry list. This causes the entry content header (right pane) to scroll out of view, breaking the reading experience.

## Expected Behavior

- Entry list should be height-constrained to the viewport
- j/k navigation should scroll only within the entry list pane
- Entry content header should always remain visible

## Current Behavior

- The `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" })` call in EntryList triggers page-level scrolling
- User loses sight of the article title/header when navigating through entries

## Root Cause Analysis

The layout structure in `application.tsx:354-402`:
- Root: `height: 100vh`, `overflow: hidden`
- EntryList container: `width: 320px`, `height: 100%`

The EntryList component (`EntryList.tsx:48-96`):
- Outer div: `h-full flex flex-col`
- Header: `h-12 shrink-0`
- ScrollArea: `flex-1`

The ScrollArea viewport (`scroll-area.tsx:17-21`):
- Has `size-full` (100% width/height)
- But may not be properly constrained by flex parent

## Potential Fix

The Radix ScrollArea needs explicit height containment. Options:

### Option A: Add overflow containment
```tsx
// In EntryList.tsx, wrap ScrollArea parent
<div className="flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden">
  <ScrollArea className="h-full">
```

The `min-h-0` is critical - flex items default to `min-height: auto` which prevents shrinking below content size.

### Option B: Use CSS overflow directly
```tsx
// Replace ScrollArea with native scroll
<div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0">
```

### Option C: Fix ScrollArea component
```tsx
// In scroll-area.tsx, add overflow: hidden to Root
<ScrollAreaPrimitive.Root
  className={cn("relative overflow-hidden", className)}
```

## Files to Modify

- `app/javascript/components/EntryList.tsx` - Add `min-h-0` to flex container
- Possibly `app/javascript/components/ui/scroll-area.tsx` - Ensure proper containment

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] j/k navigation scrolls only the entry list, not the page
- [ ] Entry content header remains visible during navigation
- [ ] Scrollbar appears on entry list when entries exceed viewport
- [ ] Mouse wheel scrolling still works within entry list
close_reason: Fixed scroll containment by adding overflow-hidden to ScrollArea root and min-h-0 to flex containers. j/k navigation now scrolls only within entry list.

title: Multi-select entries with x key for bulk actions
description:
## Summary

Add multi-select capability to the entry list using the `x` key, enabling bulk actions on selected entries.

## Concept

Use `x` key in conjunction with j/k navigation to select/deselect entries:
- **x**: Toggle selection on current entry
- **j/k**: Navigate (selection persists)
- **Shift+x** or **X**: Select range (from last selected to current)
- **Escape**: Clear all selections

## Potential Bulk Actions

Once multiple entries are selected:
- **s**: Star/unstar all selected
- **m**: Mark all selected read/unread
- **d**: Delete all selected (with confirmation)
- **Share as digest**: Export selected entries as a formatted digest (email, markdown, etc.)
- **Add label**: Apply a label to all selected
- **Move to category**: Bulk categorization

## UX Considerations

### Visual Feedback
- Selected entries need distinct visual treatment (checkbox? highlight? badge?)
- Selection count indicator in header
- Clear indication of "selection mode" vs "focus mode"

### Interaction Model Options

**Option A: Gmail-style (persistent selection)**
- x toggles selection, stays on current item
- Selection persists across navigation
- Actions apply to selection if any, otherwise current item

**Option B: Vim visual mode**
- v enters "visual/select mode"
- j/k extends selection
- Action or Escape exits mode

**Option C: Shift-based (simpler)**
- Shift+j/k extends selection from current
- No explicit x key, just shift modifiers

## Open Questions

1. Should selection persist when changing feeds/views?
2. How does selection interact with "mark all read" (existing feature)?
3. Should there be a "select all" shortcut?
4. What's the visual design for selected items?
5. How does this work with virtual scrolling (if implemented later)?
6. Share as digest - what formats? Email? Clipboard? Export file?

## Blocked

This issue is blocked pending UX design discussion. Need to:
- [ ] Decide on interaction model (Option A/B/C or hybrid)
- [ ] Design visual treatment for selected state
- [ ] Define complete list of bulk actions to support
- [ ] Consider mobile/touch implications

## Related

- Keyboard navigation (j/k) - foundation for this feature
- Bulk article actions (ttrb-391) - API support for bulk operations

title: Deep linking and URL routing system
description:
## Summary

Implement URL-based routing and deep linking to enable shareable links, browser history support, and digest email integration.

## Deep Link Types

### a) Link to a feed
```
/feeds/:id
/categories/:id
/views/fresh
/views/starred
/views/all
```

### b) Link to a specific item
```
/entries/:id
```
Opens the app with that entry selected/focused in the content pane.

### c) Link to a set of items, focused on one
```
/digest/:date          — Articles from a specific digest (by date)
/digest/:uuid          — Custom curated set of articles (shareable collection)
/entries?ids=1,2,3&focus=2
```

The UUID approach enables:
- Building a custom set of items to share
- "Share this collection" feature
- Digest emails with stable links
- Saved searches or smart folders (future)

## Open Questions

1. **URL structure**: Query params vs path segments?
   - `/entries/123` vs `/entries?id=123`
   - `/digest/2025-01-15` vs `/digest?date=2025-01-15`

2. **Collection persistence**: Where do custom collections live?
   - Database table: `collections(uuid, user_id, entry_ids[], created_at)`
   - Or ephemeral with signed/encoded IDs in URL?

3. **Auth for shared links**: 
   - Public links (no auth required)?
   - Signed URLs with expiry?
   - Login required, then redirect?

4. **State sync complexity**:
   - What state goes in URL vs stays local?
   - Sort order? Filters? Scroll position?

5. **Router choice**:
   - React Router?
   - TanStack Router?
   - Custom with History API?
   - Rails-driven (turbo frames)?

## Implementation Layers

### Layer 1: Basic routing (prerequisite for all)
- URL ↔ app state sync
- Browser back/forward
- `/feeds/:id`, `/entries/:id`, `/views/:name`

### Layer 2: Shareable entry links
- `/entries/:id` works without auth (public read?)
- Or requires auth, then redirects

### Layer 3: Collection/digest links
- Database model for collections
- `/digest/:uuid` resolves to entry set
- UI for "Share these articles"

## Depends On

- Foundational for: ttrb-weo (email digests), ttrb-i72 (multi-select share)

## Blocked

Needs design discussion before implementation:
- [ ] Decide URL structure conventions
- [ ] Decide on collection persistence model
- [ ] Decide auth model for shared links
- [ ] Choose routing library

description:
## Summary

## Network Error Scenarios

### API Failures

```typescript
test('handles feed list API failure gracefully', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/api/v1/feeds', route => route.abort())
  
  await page.goto('/')
  
  await expect(page.getByText(/error|failed|unavailable/i)).toBeVisible()
  // App should still be usable
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Settings' })).toBeEnabled()
})

test('handles entry list API failure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/')
  await page.route('**/api/v1/entries*', route => route.abort())
  
  await page.getByText('Tech News').click()
  
  await expect(page.getByText(/error|failed/i)).toBeVisible()
})

test('retries after transient failure', async ({ page }) => {
  let requestCount = 0
  await page.route('**/api/v1/feeds', route => {
    requestCount++
    if (requestCount < 2) {
      route.abort()
    } else {
      route.continue()
    }
  })
  
  await page.goto('/')
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }).click()
  
  await expect(page.getByText('Tech News')).toBeVisible()
})
```

title: Drag and drop element offset makes first folder unreachable
description:
## Summary

In the feed organizer, the dragged element visual is offset downward from the actual cursor position. This misalignment makes it impossible to drop feeds onto the first folder/category.

## Current Behavior

- When dragging a feed, the drag preview/ghost appears lower than the cursor
- Drop zone detection seems to use cursor position, but visual is offset
- Cannot drop on the first folder because the visual offset puts the "apparent" drop position below it
- Lower folders work because there's room for the offset

## Expected Behavior

- Dragged element should track directly with cursor
- Or drop zones should account for the offset
- All folders should be reachable as drop targets, including the first one

## Likely Cause

This is a common issue with dnd-kit when:
- Transform offset not calculated correctly
- Scroll position not accounted for
- Header/toolbar height throwing off calculations
- `useSortable` transform not properly applied

## Possible Fixes

1. Check dnd-kit `activatorEvent` and ensure offset is calculated from grab point
2. Use `modifiers` to adjust drag overlay position
3. Verify no CSS transforms on parent containers affecting coordinates
4. Check if scroll containers are affecting position calculation

```tsx
// Example modifier to fix offset
import { restrictToVerticalAxis, restrictToWindowEdges } from '@dnd-kit/modifiers'

<DndContext modifiers={[restrictToVerticalAxis]}>
```

## Files to Check

- `app/javascript/components/FeedOrganizer.tsx` - DndContext and useSortable usage
- Check for any CSS transforms on ancestor elements

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open Settings → Feeds (organizer)
2. Drag any feed
3. Notice the dragged element appears lower than cursor
4. Try to drop on the first category - fails because offset

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Dragged element aligns with cursor position
- [ ] Can drop on all folders including the first one
- [ ] Smooth drag experience without visual jumping
close_reason: Fixed by adding snapCenterToCursor modifier to DragOverlay. Commit c075a50.

title: Add ETag support for conditional feed requests
description:
Currently the feed fetcher only stores and uses Last-Modified headers for conditional GET requests. ETags are received from servers but discarded.

**Current behavior:**
- FeedFetcher receives ETag headers but doesn't persist them
- Only If-Modified-Since is sent on subsequent requests

**Desired behavior:**
- Store ETag values in the feeds table (add etag column)
- Send If-None-Match header with stored ETag on subsequent requests
- Handle 304 responses correctly when ETag matches

**Files to modify:**
- db/migrate/xxx_add_etag_to_feeds.rb (new)
- app/models/feed.rb
- app/services/feed_fetcher.rb
- app/services/feed_updater.rb

**References:**
- RFC 7232 (Conditional Requests)
- Current Last-Modified implementation in feed_fetcher.rb
close_reason: Added etag column to feeds table and updated FeedFetcher to send If-None-Match header. Commit 0a85f4a.

title: Add inter-request delays between feed fetches
description:
Currently feeds are fetched as fast as the Solid Queue workers can process them, with no delays between requests. This could overwhelm servers or trigger rate limiting.

**Current behavior:**
- UpdateFeedsJob enqueues all stale feeds immediately
- Worker threads (default 3) process jobs as fast as possible
- No delay between completing one fetch and starting the next

**Desired behavior:**
- Add configurable delay between feed fetch requests
- Could be implemented as a global setting or per-worker throttle
- Suggested default: 1-2 seconds between requests per worker

**Implementation options:**
1. Add sleep in UpdateFeedJob after completion
2. Use Solid Queue's scheduling to stagger job execution times
3. Implement a rate limiter service

**Files to modify:**
- app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb
- config/application.rb or new config file for throttle settings
close_reason: Added 1.5 second INTER_REQUEST_DELAY constant in UpdateFeedJob with sleep in ensure block. Commit 12b5b9a.

title: Add per-domain throttling for feed fetches
description:
If a user subscribes to multiple feeds from the same domain (e.g., 10 feeds from example.com), they could all be fetched simultaneously or in rapid succession, overwhelming that server.

**Current behavior:**
- No awareness of feed domains
- All feeds treated equally regardless of origin
- Multiple feeds from same domain can hit simultaneously across worker threads

**Desired behavior:**
- Group feeds by domain
- Enforce minimum delay between requests to the same domain
- Allow different domains to be fetched in parallel

**Implementation approach:**
1. Extract domain from feed URL
2. Use a domain-based rate limiter (could use Redis or in-memory with Concurrent::Map)
3. Before fetching, acquire a slot for that domain
4. After fetch, record timestamp for domain

**Files to modify:**
- app/services/feed_fetcher.rb or new domain_throttler.rb service
- app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb
- Possibly add redis or in-memory rate limiting gem

**Suggested minimum delay:** 5-10 seconds between requests to same domain
close_reason: Created DomainThrottler service with 5-second per-domain delay using Rails cache. Integrated into UpdateFeedJob. Commit 61ed5dc.

title: Add exponential backoff on 429 rate-limit responses
description:
When servers return 429 Too Many Requests, the app should back off and retry later rather than continuing to hammer the server.

**Current behavior:**
- 429 responses are logged as errors
- Feed's last_error is updated
- No special handling - next scheduled update will try again at normal interval

**Desired behavior:**
- Detect 429 responses specifically
- Implement exponential backoff for that feed
- Store backoff state (next_retry_at timestamp or retry_count)
- Skip feeds that are in backoff period during UpdateFeedsJob scheduling

**Implementation:**
1. Add backoff columns to feeds table (retry_after_at, consecutive_failures)
2. On 429: set retry_after_at to exponentially increasing delay (e.g., 5min, 15min, 1hr, 4hr, 24hr)
3. On success: reset backoff state
4. Modify Feed.needs_update scope to exclude feeds in backoff

**Files to modify:**
- db/migrate/xxx_add_backoff_to_feeds.rb (new)
- app/models/feed.rb (add scope, backoff methods)
- app/services/feed_fetcher.rb (detect 429)
- app/services/feed_updater.rb (apply backoff on 429)
close_reason: Implemented exponential backoff with escalating delays (5min to 24hr). Also respects Retry-After header. Commit 1032735.

title: Respect Retry-After header from server responses
description:
Servers can include a Retry-After header in 429 or 503 responses to indicate when the client should retry. Currently this header is ignored.

**Current behavior:**
- Retry-After header is not parsed or stored
- App retries at its own schedule regardless of server guidance

**Desired behavior:**
- Parse Retry-After header from 429 and 503 responses
- Retry-After can be either seconds (integer) or HTTP-date format
- Store the computed retry timestamp
- Respect server's requested delay before next fetch attempt

**Implementation:**
1. Parse Retry-After in FeedFetcher (handle both formats per RFC 7231)
2. Return retry_after value in fetch result
3. In FeedUpdater, set feed's next_retry_at based on Retry-After
4. Integrate with backoff system from 429 handling issue

**Files to modify:**
- app/services/feed_fetcher.rb (parse header)
- app/services/feed_updater.rb (apply retry timing)
- app/models/feed.rb (scope to respect retry_after)

**References:**
- RFC 7231 Section 7.1.3 (Retry-After header)
- Related to: 429 backoff issue
close_reason: Implemented as part of 429 backoff work. FeedFetcher parses Retry-After header (both integer seconds and HTTP-date formats), passes to FeedUpdater which applies it via apply_backoff! method. Commit 1032735.

title: Improve low-value component tests to be more meaningful
description:
## Summary

Several existing Vitest tests are low-value or test implementation details rather than behavior. These should be improved or removed to reduce maintenance burden and increase test value.

## Flagged Tests

### 1. api.test.ts (~60 tests) - **Most Problematic**

Nearly all tests follow this pattern:
```typescript
it("fetches feeds from GET /feeds", async () => {
  mockFetch.mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(feeds))
  const result = await api.feeds.list()
  
  expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/api/v1/feeds", {
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  })
  expect(result).toEqual(feeds)
})
```

**Problems:**
- Tests implementation (URL, headers) not behavior
- Tautological - tests that code does what code says
- Won't catch real bugs (e.g., wrong response parsing, edge cases)
- High maintenance burden when refactoring
- Better covered by E2E tests that hit real API

**Recommendation:**
- Keep only error handling tests (those are valuable)
- Remove URL/method verification tests
- Or convert to integration tests using MSW (Mock Service Worker) that test more realistic scenarios

### 2. EntryList.test.tsx - Some weak tests

**Fragile CSS assertions:**
```typescript
it("unread entries have left border indicator", () => {
  expect(entryElement).toHaveClass("border-l-2")
})
```
- Tests Tailwind class name, not visual behavior
- Breaks if styling changes but behavior is same

**Weak assertion:**
```typescript
it("handles large number of entries", () => {
  const entries = Array.from({ length: 100 }, ...)
  render(<EntryList entries={entries} />)
  expect(screen.getByText("Article 1")).toBeInTheDocument()
  expect(screen.getByText("Article 100")).toBeInTheDocument()
})
```
- Doesn't test performance, just that rendering doesn't crash
- Either add performance assertions or remove

### 3. EntryContent.test.tsx - Some weak tests

**Fragile button finding:**
```typescript
const buttons = screen.getAllByRole("button")
const prevButton = buttons[0]  // Fragile - depends on DOM order
```
- Should use accessible names or test-ids

**Implementation detail tests:**
```typescript
const circleIcon = document.querySelector("svg.lucide-circle")
expect(circleIcon).toBeInTheDocument()
```
- Tests that specific icon library class exists, not behavior
- Better: test that clicking toggles read state

## Recommended Actions

### api.test.ts
1. Delete ~50 URL/method verification tests
2. Keep error handling tests (valuable)
3. Consider adding MSW-based integration tests that:
   - Test actual fetch behavior
   - Test response parsing edge cases
   - Test network error recovery

### EntryList.test.tsx / EntryContent.test.tsx
1. Replace CSS class assertions with visual or behavioral tests
2. Use accessible queries (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) instead of DOM order
3. Remove or improve "handles large number" test
4. Test what users see/do, not implementation details

## Test Quality Principles

Good tests:
- ✅ Test behavior, not implementation
- ✅ Use accessible queries
- ✅ Break when behavior breaks, not when refactoring
- ✅ Provide documentation of expected behavior

Bad tests:
- ❌ Verify URL strings and headers
- ❌ Check CSS class names
- ❌ Find elements by DOM position
- ❌ Test internal state

## Estimated Impact

- Remove/improve ~60-70 tests
- Reduce maintenance burden
- Increase confidence in remaining tests
- Make refactoring easier

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] api.test.ts reduced to meaningful tests only
- [ ] EntryList/EntryContent tests use accessible queries
- [ ] No tests checking Tailwind class names
- [ ] No tests finding buttons by index
- [ ] Test count may decrease, but test value increases

title: OPML preview endpoint accidentally imports feeds
description:
## Bug

When selecting an OPML file to preview before importing, all feeds show as 'already subscribed' even on first import. The preview UI shows '0 new, 152 already subscribed'.

## Root Cause

`opml_controller.rb:40` in the `preview` action:

```ruby
def preview
  opml_content = params[:file].read
  importer = OpmlImporter.new(current_user, opml_content)
  result = importer.import  # <-- BUG: This actually creates the feeds!
  
  existing_urls = current_user.feeds.pluck(:feed_url).to_set  # Now all exist!
  # ...
end
```

The preview endpoint calls `importer.import` which creates all the feeds in the database. Then when it checks `existing_urls`, they all exist because they were just imported.

## Impact

- **Data corruption**: Feeds are silently imported during 'preview'
- **Confusing UX**: User sees all feeds as 'already subscribed'
- **Import button disabled**: Since new_feeds=0, import button is grayed out
- **Duplicate import impossible**: Re-selecting file still shows all as existing

## Fix

The OpmlImporter needs a separate parse-only method:

```ruby
# In opml_importer.rb
def parse
  # Just parse and return ImportedFeed objects without database operations
end

def import
  # Existing implementation that creates feeds
end
```

Then in the controller:

```ruby
def preview
  result = importer.parse  # <-- Parse only, don't import
  existing_urls = current_user.feeds.pluck(:feed_url).to_set
  # Compare against actually existing feeds
end
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Preview only parses OPML, does not create feeds
- [ ] Existing feed detection works correctly against DB state before preview
- [ ] Clicking 'Import X Feeds' actually imports them
- [ ] Re-selecting same file shows correct new/existing counts
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace waitForTimeout with proper auto-waiting in E2E tests
description:
The Playwright testing guide explicitly forbids hard waits (waitForTimeout). Currently ~100+ instances across all test files use waitForTimeout for arbitrary delays. Replace these with proper auto-waiting patterns:

**Files affected (all in e2e/):**
- auth.spec.ts (1 instance)
- feed-management.spec.ts (4 instances)  
- article-reading.spec.ts (4 instances)
- keyboard-navigation.spec.ts (~35 instances)
- command-palette.spec.ts (6 instances)
- settings.spec.ts (5 instances)
- filters-labels.spec.ts (8 instances)
- error-handling.spec.ts (~20 instances)
- fixtures/auth.ts (1 instance in waitForAppReady)

**Replacement strategies:**
1. Use web-first assertions that auto-retry: `await expect(element).toBeVisible()`
2. Use `waitFor` on specific elements: `await element.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })`
3. Wait for network requests: `await page.waitForResponse(resp => ...)`
4. For animations, use `await expect(dialog).toHaveCSS('opacity', '1')`

**Example before:**
```typescript
await page.keyboard.press('j')
await page.waitForTimeout(200)
```

**Example after:**
```typescript
await page.keyboard.press('j')
// Wait for visible state change indicating navigation occurred
await expect(page.getByTestId('entry-item').first()).toHaveAttribute('data-selected', 'true')
```
close_reason: All waitForTimeout instances removed from E2E tests. Replaced with proper Playwright auto-waiting patterns. All 203 tests pass.

title: Implement Page Object Model for E2E tests
description:
The Playwright testing guide recommends using the Page Object Model (POM) pattern to organize tests and avoid duplicating locators. Currently all tests use direct page locators.

**Recommended structure:**
```
e2e/
├── pages/
│   ├── feeds.page.ts      # Feed sidebar, entry list, content area
│   ├── settings.page.ts   # Settings dialog with all tabs
│   ├── command-palette.page.ts
│   └── components/
│       ├── sidebar.component.ts
│       ├── entry-list.component.ts
│       └── dialog.component.ts
├── fixtures/
│   └── test.ts            # Custom test fixtures
├── tests/
│   └── *.spec.ts          # Test files using page objects
└── playwright.config.ts
```

**Example page object (from guide):**
```typescript
// e2e/pages/feeds.page.ts
export class FeedsPage {
  readonly page: Page
  readonly sidebar: Locator
  readonly entryList: Locator
  readonly refreshButton: Locator

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.page = page
    this.sidebar = page.getByTestId('feed-sidebar')
    this.entryList = page.getByTestId('entry-list')
    this.refreshButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh' })
  }

  async goto() { await this.page.goto('/') }
  async selectFeed(name: string) { ... }
  async refresh() { ... }
}
```

**Benefits:**
- Centralized locator definitions (single place to update)
- Reusable actions across tests
- Better readability and maintainability
- Encapsulates complex interactions

title: Replace document.querySelector with accessible queries in tests

title: Replace fireEvent with userEvent in CommandPalette.test.tsx
description:
The useCommandPalette hook tests use fireEvent.keyDown for keyboard events instead of userEvent.

**Best Practice Violation:**
The guide states: 'Always prefer userEvent - it simulates real user interactions'

**Files Affected:**
- CommandPalette.test.tsx (lines 387-421): useCommandPalette tests use fireEvent.keyDown

**Fix:**
Replace fireEvent.keyDown with userEvent.keyboard:
```typescript
// Before
fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: 'k', ctrlKey: true })

// After  
const user = userEvent.setup()
await user.keyboard('{Control>}k{/Control}')
```
close_reason: Won't fix: fireEvent.keyDown(document, ...) is the correct pattern for testing hooks that add document-level keyboard event listeners. userEvent.keyboard() dispatches to the focused element, not document, making it unsuitable for this use case.

comments.author: andy
comments.text:
After investigation, I found that using fireEvent.keyDown(document, {...}) for the useCommandPalette hook tests is actually the appropriate approach in this case:

1. The hook adds an event listener directly to `document` for global keyboard shortcuts
2. `userEvent.keyboard()` dispatches events to the focused element, not document
3. When using `renderHook()`, there's no focusable DOM element to receive the events
4. The Vitest/RTL guide says to use fireEvent "when userEvent doesn't support the interaction"

For document-level keyboard shortcuts in hook tests, fireEvent is the correct tool. The tests are already written correctly - this issue can be closed as "won't fix" or converted to documentation clarifying when fireEvent is appropriate.

title: Improve weak assertions in E2E error handling tests

Many tests in `error-handling.spec.ts` use `await expect(page.locator('body')).toBeVisible()` as their only assertion. This just verifies the page didn't crash, not that error handling worked correctly.

title: Switch from Solid Queue to GoodJob
description:
Replace Solid Queue with GoodJob for background job processing. GoodJob is PostgreSQL-native and supports async (in-process) execution mode that works with Passenger/Phusion, unlike Solid Queue's Puma-only plugin.

**Why Switch:**
- Using PostgreSQL, so GoodJob's Postgres-native approach is a better fit
- Need in-process job execution with Passenger (Solid Queue's plugin is Puma-only)
- GoodJob has built-in cron/recurring job support that works in async mode

**Migration Steps:**

1. Update Gemfile:
   - Remove: gem 'solid_queue'
   - Add: gem 'good_job'

2. Run generator:
   ```
   bin/rails g good_job:install
   bin/rails db:migrate
   ```

3. Configure config/application.rb or environment files:
   ```ruby
   config.active_job.queue_adapter = :good_job
   config.good_job.execution_mode = :async
   config.good_job.enable_cron = true
   ```

4. Migrate recurring jobs from config/recurring.yml to GoodJob cron format:
   ```ruby
   config.good_job.cron = {
     update_feeds: {
       cron: '*/5 * * * *',  # every 5 minutes
       class: 'UpdateFeedsJob'
     },
     purge_articles: {
       cron: '0 3 * * *',  # at 3am daily
       class: 'PurgeArticlesJob'
     }
   }
   ```

5. Remove Solid Queue config:
   - Delete config/recurring.yml
   - Remove solid_queue plugin from config/puma.rb
   - Remove db/queue_schema.rb (or migrate data first)

6. Optional: Enable GoodJob dashboard in routes.rb:
   ```ruby
   mount GoodJob::Engine => '/good_job'
   ```

**Files to Modify:**
- Gemfile
- config/application.rb or config/environments/*.rb
- config/routes.rb (optional dashboard)
- config/puma.rb (remove solid_queue plugin)
- Remove config/recurring.yml

**Notes:**
- GoodJob needs ~2 extra DB connections for cron in async mode
- Jobs won't start until first web request (Rails autoloading)
- Consider keeping existing jobs in queue during migration
close_reason: Already completed: GoodJob is configured in Gemfile, config/initializers/good_job.rb, and environment files. Solid Queue has been removed. Migration complete.

title: Adaptive feed polling based on publication frequency
description:
Dynamically adjust feed polling intervals based on how frequently each feed actually publishes new content. This reduces unnecessary requests to slow feeds while keeping high-volume feeds fresh.

**Current Behavior:**
All feeds are polled on the same fixed interval (every 5 minutes via UpdateFeedsJob).

**Desired Behavior:**
Track publication patterns and adjust polling frequency per-feed:
- High-frequency feeds (multiple posts/day): Poll every 5-15 minutes
- Medium-frequency feeds (daily): Poll every 1-2 hours  
- Low-frequency feeds (weekly/monthly): Poll every 6-24 hours
- Dead/inactive feeds: Poll once per day or less

**Implementation Approach:**

1. Add tracking columns to feeds table:
   ```ruby
   add_column :feeds, :avg_posts_per_day, :float, default: 0
   add_column :feeds, :last_new_entry_at, :datetime
   add_column :feeds, :calculated_interval, :integer  # seconds
   add_column :feeds, :next_poll_at, :datetime
   ```

2. Update statistics after each feed refresh:
   - Track rolling average of posts per day (e.g., last 30 days)
   - Calculate optimal interval based on frequency
   - Set next_poll_at = now + calculated_interval

3. Modify UpdateFeedsJob to poll selectively:
   ```ruby
   Feed.where('next_poll_at <= ?', Time.current).find_each do |feed|
     UpdateFeedJob.perform_later(feed.id)
   end
   ```

4. Algorithm considerations:
   - Minimum interval: 5 minutes (respect server resources)
   - Maximum interval: 24 hours (ensure eventual freshness)
   - Factor in feed errors (back off on repeated failures)
   - Allow manual override per feed (update_interval already exists)
   - New feeds start with aggressive polling until pattern established

**Bonus Features:**
- Respect HTTP Cache-Control / Expires headers
- Use HTTP conditional requests (If-Modified-Since, ETag)
- Track and honor retry-after on 429/503 responses

**Files to Modify:**
- db/migrate/xxx_add_adaptive_polling_to_feeds.rb
- app/models/feed.rb - Add interval calculation logic
- app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb - Update stats after refresh
- app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb - Query by next_poll_at
close_reason: Already implemented: migration exists, Feed model has interval calculation (calculate_avg_posts_per_day, calculate_optimal_interval), FeedUpdater calls update_polling_stats!, UpdateFeedsJob queries by next_poll_at. All tests pass.

title: Improve test suite performance
description:
As the test suite grows, we need to ensure tests remain fast enough for a good developer experience.

**Current Test Suite:**
- Rails/Minitest: 2 test files
- Vitest (component tests): 18 test files
- Playwright (E2E tests): 9 spec files

**Potential Optimizations:**

**Vitest:**
- Enable parallel test execution (--pool=threads or --pool=forks)
- Use vi.mock hoisting efficiently
- Consider test sharding for CI: vitest --shard=1/3
- Profile slow tests: vitest --reporter=verbose
- Lazy load heavy dependencies in tests

**Playwright:**
- Run tests in parallel (already default, but tune workers)
- Use test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' }) where safe
- Reuse authentication state across tests (storageState)
- Consider sharding for CI: --shard=1/3
- Use API calls for setup instead of UI interactions

**Rails/Minitest:**
- Use parallel test workers: PARALLEL_WORKERS=4 bin/rails test
- Use fixtures instead of factories where possible
- Profile with: bin/rails test --profile
- Consider spring for faster boot: bin/rails test (with spring binstub)

**CI-specific:**
- Cache node_modules and bundle between runs
- Run test types in parallel jobs (Rails, Vitest, Playwright)
- Use test splitting services (e.g., CircleCI test splitting)
- Store and compare test timing data

**Measurement:**
Before optimizing, establish baselines:
- npm run test (Vitest)
- npm run test:e2e (Playwright)
- bin/rails test (Minitest)

Track these in CI to catch regressions.
close_reason: Test suite already well optimized. Fixed Vitest 4.x deprecation warning. Baselines: Vitest 4s/492 tests, Playwright 36s/209 tests, Rails 6s/77 tests. All already use parallel execution.

title: Investigate: Manual refresh may bypass fetch intervals (429 rate limit hit)

title: Create SendDigestsJob for scheduled delivery
description:
Create the background job that sends digest emails at each user's preferred time.

## SendDigestsJob
- Runs hourly via GoodJob cron
- Checks which users should receive digests now
- Sends emails in batches to avoid overwhelming mail server

## Logic
1. Find users where:
   - `email` is present and valid
   - `email_digest` preference is true
   - `digest_preferred_time` matches current hour (with timezone handling)
   - `last_digest_sent` is nil or > 23 hours ago
2. For each user:
   - Check if they have unread articles meeting criteria
   - If yes, send DigestMailer.digest_email(user)
   - Update user.last_digest_sent
   - Optionally mark articles as read if digest_catchup is true
3. Log summary

## GoodJob Cron Entry
Add to `config/initializers/good_job.rb`:
```ruby
send_digests: {
  cron: "0 * * * *", # every hour at minute 0
  class: "SendDigestsJob",
  description: "Send email digests to users at their preferred time"
}
```

## Timezone Handling
- Store preferred time in user's timezone or UTC
- Compare with current hour in that timezone

## Error Handling
- Catch and log delivery failures per user
- Don't let one failure stop other users' digests
- Consider retry logic for transient failures

## Files to Create/Modify
- `app/jobs/send_digests_job.rb`
- `config/initializers/good_job.rb` - Add cron entry

## Testing
- Unit tests for user selection logic
- Test that digest_catchup marks articles read

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Job runs hourly without error
- [ ] Users receive emails at their preferred time
- [ ] last_digest_sent is updated after sending
- [ ] Articles marked read if digest_catchup enabled
- [ ] Failures for one user don't affect others
close_reason: SendDigestsJob with GoodJob cron, user selection logic, catchup support

title: Implement responsive three-pane layout
description:
Convert the fixed three-pane layout to a responsive design.

## Current State

  - Navigation via bottom tabs or hamburger menu
- **Tablet (640px - 1024px)**: Two panes

### Option B: Layout Context

  - `currentPane: 'sidebar' | 'list' | 'content'`

title: Extend API to support multi-column sorting
description:
Update the entries API to support sorting by multiple columns.

## Current API
```
GET /api/entries?order_by=date|score
```
Only supports single column sort.

## New API Format
```
GET /api/entries?sort=date:desc,feed:asc,score:desc
```
Comma-separated list of column:direction pairs.

## Supported Columns
- `date` - entries.date_entered or entries.published (TBD)
- `feed` - feeds.title
- `title` - entries.title
- `score` - user_entries.score
- `unread` - user_entries.unread (boolean, unread first = desc)

## Implementation

### Parse Sort Parameter
```ruby
def parse_sort_param(sort_string)
  return [{ column: 'date', direction: 'desc' }] if sort_string.blank?
  
  sort_string.split(',').map do |part|
    column, direction = part.split(':')
    { column: column, direction: direction || 'desc' }
  end
end
```

### Build ORDER BY Clause
Map column names to SQL:
- Validate columns against allowlist
- Sanitize direction (only 'asc' or 'desc')
- Join with ORDER BY

### Backwards Compatibility
- Keep supporting `order_by` param for now
- If both present, `sort` takes precedence

## Files to Modify
- `app/controllers/api/v1/entries_controller.rb`
  - Update `index` action
  - Update `feed_entries` action
  - Add `parse_sort_param` private method

## Testing
- Test multi-column sort produces correct order
- Test invalid columns are ignored
- Test SQL injection protection
- Test backwards compatibility

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sort=date:desc,feed:asc` works correctly
- [ ] Invalid columns are ignored safely
- [ ] No SQL injection possible
- [ ] Old `order_by` param still works
close_reason: Implemented multi-column sorting in entries API

title: Implement word frequency analysis for feed content
description:

3. Store/cache results for feeds
4. Expose via API endpoint

### API
- `GET /api/v1/feeds/:id/word_frequency` - Get top keywords for a feed
- `GET /api/v1/articles/:id/keywords` - Get keywords for an article

title: Click word in frequency list to create/remove tagging filter
description:
## Problem
Word frequency analysis shows relevant keywords, but creating filters from them is manual.

## Solution
Make word frequency list interactive for quick filter creation.

### Behavior

**Unhighlighted word (no filter exists):**
- Click → Create filter that:
  - Matches articles containing that word
  - Tags articles with that word
- Word becomes highlighted
- Tagged articles appear in virtual folder for that tag

**Highlighted word (filter exists):**
- Click → Remove the filter
- Existing tags remain on articles (not deleted)
- Word becomes unhighlighted

### Visual Design
- Highlighted words: distinct style (background color, bold, etc.)
- Clickable appearance (cursor, hover state)
- Maybe tooltip: "Click to create/remove filter"

### Dependencies
- ttrb-bk55: Unified feed dialog (word frequency lives here)

- Virtual folders for tagged items

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Click unhighlighted word → creates tagging filter
- [ ] Filter matches word in content, applies word as tag
- [ ] Word becomes highlighted when filter exists
- [ ] Click highlighted word → removes filter
- [ ] Existing tags preserved when filter removed
- [ ] Tagged items visible in virtual folder
close_reason: Implemented clickable word frequency tags that create/remove tagging filters. Added visual highlighting, tooltips, and tests.

title: Add filter backfill to apply filters to existing articles
description:
## Problem
Filters only apply to new articles when they arrive. Existing articles aren't tagged/processed.

## Solution
Option to backfill (apply filter to existing articles) when creating or editing a filter.

### Behavior
- When creating/saving a filter, offer: "Apply to existing articles?"
- If yes, run filter against all existing articles matching scope
- Apply actions (tag, mark read, score, etc.) to matches
- Show progress/count of affected articles

### Considerations
- Could be slow for large article counts
- Maybe run as background job with progress indicator
- Destructive actions (delete, mark read) may need confirmation
- Scope limiting helps (feed/category scoped filters = fewer articles)

### UI Options
- Checkbox on filter save: "Apply to existing articles"
- Separate "Run now" button on filter list
- Both

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Option to apply filter to existing articles
- [ ] Runs filter logic against historical articles
- [ ] Actions applied to matching articles
- [ ] Progress feedback for large backfills
- [ ] Handles destructive actions appropriately
close_reason: Filter backfill feature implemented with API endpoint, UI button, and rake tasks. One-time initialization complete.

```yaml
sync-branch: beads-sync
```

```ruby
ACTION_MARK_READ = 2

```

String enum (Rails enum with string values or similar):
```ruby
enum action_type: {

  mark_read: 'mark_read',
  star: 'star',
  tag: 'tag',
  # etc.
}
```

## Benefits
- Self-documenting in database
- Easier debugging
- No magic numbers
- Clearer API responses

## Scope

- Possibly filter_type (rule types) as well if same pattern

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Migration to convert existing integer values
- [ ] All references updated

close_reason: Migrated action_type from integer constants to string enum. Database now stores human-readable strings like 'mark_read' instead of magic numbers.

title: Set up automated PostgreSQL backups via pg_dump cron job
description:
## Context
Nibbler uses PostgreSQL via Kamal accessory. Data lives in Docker volume `nibbler-db-data`.

## Requirements
- Daily pg_dump backup
- Store backups in a persistent location (Drobo or cloud)
- Keep N days of rolling backups (e.g., 7 days)
- Consider compression (gzip)

## Implementation options
1. Cron job on host running `docker exec nibbler-db pg_dump`
2. Backup script in docker-services directory for reproducibility
3. Optional: sync to cloud storage (Backblaze B2, S3, etc.)

## Example
```bash
0 3 * * * docker exec nibbler-db pg_dump -U nibbler nibbler_production | gzip > /backup/nibbler-$(date +\%Y\%m\%d).sql.gz
```

title: Follow Story: absorb newswatch into nibbler
description:
Add a 'Follow this story' action to nibbler entries that creates an ongoing tracked story. Absorbs newswatch functionality (~/projects/newswatch) into nibbler as a first-class feature.

## Why absorb (vs shell out)
Split-brain problem: newswatch has its own SQLite DB and CLI-only UI. If nibbler is the primary reading surface, story updates should show up there. Absorbing avoids a second app + second DB + separate briefing email.

## LLM backend: Ollama on baru
- baru (192.168.1.196) runs Ollama with GPU, idle overnight
- http://baru:11434 -- Ollama bound to LAN
- No accessory container needed; nibbler makes outbound HTTP calls
- Default model: gemma4:e4b (8B) -- tested 2026-04-13, 132 t/s, correct verdict on analyze task. Bigger models (mistral-small3.2, gemma4:31b) were slower AND worse: mistral got 'concluded' wrong, gemma4:31b emitted duplicate JSON keys.
- Model swappable via OLLAMA_MODEL env var

## Scope (two LLM tasks)
1. Query extraction: given an Entry, produce topic name + ~3 search queries for follow-up coverage
2. Analyze: given prior story summary + new articles, decide if something substantively new happened (JSON: new_development, concluded, timeline_label, updated_summary, rationale)

## Data source
Google News RSS per query (same as newswatch). Articles dedup by URL per story.

## Scheduling
Overnight batch. baru is free at night. Latency is a non-issue at ~1.5s generation per analyze call.

title: LlmClient service with Ollama backend
description:
Add `app/services/llm_client.rb` that wraps HTTP calls to Ollama's /api/generate.

## Interface
```ruby
LlmClient.new(model: ENV.fetch('OLLAMA_MODEL', 'gemma4:e4b'))
  .generate(prompt:, format: :json, timeout: 120)
# returns parsed hash if format: :json, string otherwise
```

## Env vars
- OLLAMA_URL (default http://baru:11434 -- or http://host.docker.internal:11434 for local dev)
- OLLAMA_MODEL (default gemma4:e4b)

## Error handling
- Raise LlmClient::Unreachable if baru is down -- callers (jobs) retry tomorrow
- Raise LlmClient::BadJson if format: :json and response doesn't parse
- Log slow calls (>30s)

## Tests
- Stub Net::HTTP for unit tests
- Integration test skipped unless OLLAMA_URL reachable

- NOT NULL on user_id, name, created_at
- Unique index (story_id, url) on story_articles
- Index story_analyses on (story_id, created_at)

title: Resolve uncommitted Gemfile/Gemfile.lock drift (puma pin bump + broad lock re-resolve)
description:
The working tree has uncommitted dependency changes of unknown provenance.

Gemfile: puma pin changed from '>= 5.0' to '~> 7.1'
Gemfile.lock: 203 insertions / 173 deletions, which is a wider re-resolve than a puma bump alone accounts for.

These were not present at the start of the 2026-08-17 triage session and were not produced by it. Likely another session in the same checkout, mid-update.

Acceptance criteria:
- Determine whether the change is intentional and complete
- Run the full test suite against the new lock
- Verify puma 7.x boots under the Kamal/production config before committing
- Either commit with a real message or revert the tree to a clean state
close_reason: Drift was already resolved before this issue was worked: it is the working tree that became c932a46 (Gemfile 1/1, Gemfile.lock 203/173 vs parent 636193f, matching this ticket's numbers exactly), finished by 277d070 which restored the puma pin to >= 5.0 and moved the lock to puma 8.0.2. Net Gemfile diff zero, tree clean. Verified against HEAD: Minitest 359 runs/993 assertions/0 failures, RuboCop 0 offenses, bundler-audit 0 vulns, production boot via rails runner OK, and docker build --platform linux/amd64 exit 0 proving the re-resolved lock installs frozen on the deploy arch. Puma 8's IPv6 bind breaking change is handled by puma's own fallback. Residual: puma 8 serving a live request is still unverified, as it needs a server process. Filed ttrb-ad1w and ttrb-kjya from findings.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Drift was resolved by another session before this work started. Tree is clean for Gemfile/Gemfile.lock; the changes landed as c932a46 (security sweep, 163 advisories -> 0) and 277d070 (puma 7.2.1 -> 8.0.2, Gemfile pin restored to >= 5.0 so net Gemfile diff is zero).

Independent re-verification:
- git diff HEAD -- Gemfile Gemfile.lock: empty
- bundle check: dependencies satisfied
- Full Minitest suite: 359 runs, 993 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips
- config/puma.rb parses under puma 8.0.2: dev 3/3 threads, tcp://[::]:3000, 0 workers; with PORT=80 RAILS_MAX_THREADS=5 WEB_CONCURRENCY=2 RAILS_ENV=production -> 5/5 threads, 2 workers, tcp://[::]:80
- Gemfile.lock PLATFORMS includes x86_64-linux and x86_64-linux-gnu, matching deploy.yml builder arch: amd64

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Provenance confirmed exactly. c932a46 against its parent 636193f is:
  Gemfile       1 insertion / 1 deletion  (puma '>= 5.0' -> '~> 7.1')
  Gemfile.lock  203 insertions / 173 deletions

Those are precisely the numbers in this ticket's description, so the uncommitted drift observed during triage was the working tree that became c932a46. Not unknown provenance, and not abandoned work. It was then finished by 049fff5 (npm) and 277d070, which restored the Gemfile pin to '>= 5.0' and moved the lock to puma 8.0.2. Net Gemfile diff across the whole sequence is zero.

Verification run against HEAD 968683b:
  git diff HEAD -- Gemfile Gemfile.lock     empty
  bundle check                              satisfied
  Minitest                                  359 runs, 993 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips
  RuboCop                                   173 files, 0 offenses
  bundler-audit (DB updated 2026-08-16)     0 vulnerabilities
  rails runner, RAILS_ENV=production        Rails 8.1.3.1 boots, good_job async config applies, puma 8.0.2 loads
  docker build --platform linux/amd64       exit 0, image exported

The docker build is the meaningful check on the 203/173 re-resolve: it runs bundle install under BUNDLE_DEPLOYMENT=1 (frozen) on linux/amd64 and then assets:precompile. Both succeeded, so the lock is installable on the deploy target. Gemfile.lock PLATFORMS carries x86_64-linux and x86_64-linux-gnu, matching deploy.yml builder arch: amd64.

On the puma 8 major specifically: 8.0.0's one breaking change is the default production bind moving from 0.0.0.0 to ::. config/puma.rb never sets a host, so it inherits that default. Not a risk here. Puma::Configuration#clamp calls rewrite_unavailable_ipv6_binds!, which rewrites tcp://[::]:PORT back to tcp://0.0.0.0:PORT when Socket.getifaddrs finds no non-loopback IPv6 interface (configuration.rb:290, 401-424). A container without IPv6 falls back rather than failing to bind. Also note 8.0 added Puma::Configuration::NotClampedError, so options must be read after clamp; only affects code reading the config directly, not the app.

RESIDUAL, unchanged from 277d070: puma 8 still has not been shown to serve an HTTP request here. Closing that gap means starting a server process (the image CMD is ./bin/thrust ./bin/rails server), which I do not do unprompted. Everything short of that is now verified, including a successful production image build. Worth one manual boot before the next deploy.

Discovered and filed, not fixed here: ttrb-ad1w (P1, .dockerignore gap making the image 10.8GB) and ttrb-kjya (P1, .kamal/secrets unignored). ttrb-w6o3 and ttrb-k1qa already covered the SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA and async-jobs findings.

title: Add engines field to package.json to match .node-version
description:
.node-version specifies 25.4.0 but package.json has no 'engines' field, so npm will not warn or fail when someone installs under a different major.

Acceptance criteria:
- package.json declares an engines.node range consistent with .node-version 25.4.0
- Decide whether to set engine-strict in .npmrc
close_reason: package.json declares engines.node ^25.4.0, matching the .node-version 25.4.0 pin. engine-strict decided against and recorded in a new .npmrc: the check is tree-wide, so it would turn any dependency's stale/closed engines range into a hard install failure, which is a live hazard on an odd-numbered Node line. Warn-not-fail behavior verified empirically on npm 11.7.0 under Node 25.4.0 (EBADENGINE warn + exit 0; exit 1 with --engine-strict). Build and 544 vitest tests green. Commit 6561550.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 6561550: added engines.node ^25.4.0 to package.json and a .npmrc recording the engine-strict decision.

VERIFIED (npm 11.7.0 under Node 25.4.0, the version .node-version pins)
- Root package engines ARE checked. Scratch package with engines.node ^24.0.0 on Node 25.4.0: default install prints 'npm warn EBADENGINE ... required: { node: ^24.0.0 } current: { node: v25.4.0 }' and exits 0; the same install with --engine-strict exits 1 with 'npm error code EBADENGINE'. So the field delivers exactly the warn-not-fail signal this issue asked for.
- Mechanism, read in source rather than assumed: @npmcli/arborist build-ideal-tree.js #checkEngineAndPlatform iterates idealTree.inventory and calls npm-install-checks checkEngine on every non-optional node, then either throws (engineStrict) or log.warn's. The loop covers the root node and every dependency alike.
- ^25.4.0 covers .node-version: semver.satisfies('25.4.0', '^25.4.0') true; current node 25.4.0 satisfies.
- Project install clean: npm install --dry-run exits 0 with zero EBADENGINE lines, and so does --dry-run --engine-strict.
- Scanned the whole installed tree: 0 packages declare an engines.node range excluding 25.4.0. 34 distinct ranges present; the 10 enumerated (||) ones all end in an open >= clause, e.g. '^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=24.0.0' and '^22.20 || ^24.12 || >=25'.
- npm run build exit 0; npm run test:run 28 files / 544 tests passed.

DECISION: engine-strict=false, written to .npmrc with the reasoning rather than left implicit.
The check is tree-wide, not root-only, so turning it on converts any dependency's stale or closed engines range into a hard install failure. Ranges that enumerate LTS majors without an open upper bound ('^20 || ^22 || ^24') exclude an odd-numbered line like 25, so on Node 25 that is a live hazard from third-party metadata alone. Today's tree does pass with engine-strict on, so this is about future dependency churn, not a present failure. Real enforcement already exists where it matters: Dockerfile ARG NODE_VERSION=25.4.0 and three CI jobs using actions/setup-node with node-version-file.

NOTES
- Only engines.node was added. engines.npm was left out as out of scope; Node 25.4.0 bundles npm 11.7.0.
- Dockerfile:54-55 copies only package.json and package-lock.json before npm ci, so the new .npmrc does not reach the image build and cannot change it. Behavior there is npm's default, which is the same value.
- Coupling introduced: a future .node-version bump must also bump engines.node or npm ci starts warning. That is the intended guardrail, but it is a fourth place the version now lives.
- Methodology warning for anyone repeating this: nodenv resolves per-directory, and scratch dirs outside this repo picked up the global 24.13.0 instead of 25.4.0. My first round of checks silently ran on the wrong Node and showed no warning at all. Redone with a .node-version in the scratch dir; only those results are quoted above.
