title: Feeds do not auto-refresh: diagnose why UpdateFeedsJob 5-min GoodJob cron is not producing new entries
description:
A manual click of the refresh button is currently required to get new entries (Fresh folder stays stale). But automatic refresh is already supposed to be wired up:

config/initializers/good_job.rb:6 registers an `update_feeds` cron entry running `UpdateFeedsJob` every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`). UpdateFeedsJob (app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb) selects feeds due per adaptive polling (next_poll_at) and enqueues UpdateFeedJob for each.

So this is a bug (scheduler not actually running), not a missing feature.

Prime suspects:
1. Development: config/environments/development.rb:58 sets `good_job.execution_mode = :external`. Under :external the Rails web process runs NO jobs and NO cron scheduler; only an external `bin/jobs` process does. Procfile.dev includes `jobs: bin/jobs`, so cron only fires when the app is started via `bin/dev`. Starting `rails server` alone means zero background execution -> manual refresh is the only path.
2. Production: config/environments/production.rb:51 sets `execution_mode = :async` with `max_threads = 2`, running jobs inside the Puma process. config/deploy.yml:11-14 has the dedicated `job:` server block commented out, so there is no separate worker host. Async-in-web is fragile: work dies on container restart and competes with request threads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Determine empirically whether the update_feeds cron is enqueuing in each environment (inspect GoodJob::Job / good_job_cron_entries or the GoodJob dashboard; check last enqueue timestamps for UpdateFeedsJob).
- Identify which of the above (or a third cause, e.g. adaptive polling next_poll_at never advancing, or feeds stuck behind retry_after) is actually blocking refresh.
- Document the finding on this issue before fixing.

Affected files:
- config/initializers/good_job.rb
- config/environments/development.rb, config/environments/production.rb
- config/deploy.yml
- app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb, app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb
- Procfile.dev
close_reason: Diagnosed. Two independent causes. DEV: cron never runs, execution_mode=:external needs bin/jobs; last GoodJob process heartbeat 2026-01-21 (7 months stale). PROD: cron fires correctly every 5 min (suspect #2 refuted), but every UpdateFeedJob dies at domain_throttler.rb:14 with PG::UndefinedTable solid_cache_entries, before FeedUpdater is ever reached, so next_poll_at never advances and the same 73 feeds requeue forever. Manual refresh works because the controller calls FeedUpdater directly, bypassing DomainThrottler/Rails.cache. Cache table missing because database.yml's cache: entry inherits url: DATABASE_URL (overriding database: nibbler_production_cache, both resolve to nibbler_production) and migrations_paths points at a nonexistent db/cache_migrate. Fixes filed: ttrb-sqvo (P0), ttrb-6mi0, ttrb-u55y, ttrb-771g, ttrb-q19b, ttrb-w6o3, ttrb-rod2.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE. Two independent causes, one per environment. Suspect #1 confirmed for dev; suspect #2 refuted for prod; the real prod blocker is a third cause not in the original list.

== DEVELOPMENT: cron never runs (suspect #1 CONFIRMED) ==
Newest UpdateFeedsJob record: 2026-01-21 13:30:12 UTC. Current time 2026-08-17. Nothing for 7 months.
GoodJob::Process.count == 1, and it is a stale record: proctitle "bin/jobs", hostname "iris", last heartbeat 2026-01-21 13:30:13.
execution_mode = :external (config/environments/development.rb:58), so `rails server` alone runs zero jobs and zero cron. Only `bin/dev` (Procfile.dev -> `jobs: bin/jobs`) starts the scheduler.
Right now `UpdateFeedsJob.new.send(:feeds_to_update).count` == 72 of 72 feeds due, all with next_poll_at in January. The work is queued up and nothing is there to run it.

== PRODUCTION: cron runs fine (suspect #2 REFUTED) ==
execution_mode = :async inside Puma works. From `bin/kamal app logs`, UpdateFeedsJob fires exactly on the */5 boundary:
  21:50:02, 21:55:02, 22:00:02, 22:05:02, 22:10:00
Each of the first four enqueued 73 distinct feeds. The scheduler is not the problem.

== PRODUCTION ROOT CAUSE (third cause, not in the original suspect list) ==
Every UpdateFeedJob dies before it ever fetches anything:

  ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid (PG::UndefinedTable: ERROR: relation "solid_cache_entries" does not exist)
    app/services/domain_throttler.rb:14:in 'DomainThrottler.wait_for'
    app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb:26:in 'UpdateFeedJob#perform'

291 occurrences in a ~25 minute log window. domain_throttler.rb:14 is `Rails.cache.read(cache_key(domain))`, and production.rb:45 sets `cache_store = :solid_cache_store`.

update_feed_job.rb:26 (`DomainThrottler.wait_for`) runs BEFORE line 28 (`FeedUpdater.new(feed).update`), so the feed is never fetched, update_polling_stats! never runs, and next_poll_at never advances. The same 73 feeds come due again 5 minutes later. Infinite no-op loop, zero new entries, forever.

`retry_on StandardError, attempts: 3` explains the enqueue pattern: 73 distinct feed ids but 219 enqueue lines per cycle (one initial + two retries each), all three failing identically.

Why manual refresh works: Api::V1::FeedsController#refresh calls `FeedUpdater.new(@feed).update` directly and never touches DomainThrottler, so it never touches Rails.cache. That is the entire difference between the working path and the broken one.

== WHY solid_cache_entries DOES NOT EXIST ==
config/database.yml production `cache:` inherits `url: <%= ENV["DATABASE_URL"] %>` from &primary_production, and that url overrides the explicit `database: nibbler_production_cache`. Verified by resolving the real config:

  $ DATABASE_URL=postgres://.../nibbler_production bin/rails runner -e production \
      'ActiveRecord::Base.configurations.configs_for(env_name: "production").each { |c| ... }'
  name=primary  database="nibbler_production"  migrations_paths=nil
  name=cache    database="nibbler_production"  migrations_paths="db/cache_migrate"

Both resolve to the SAME database. Additionally `db/cache_migrate` does not exist on disk (only db/cache_schema.rb, which defines solid_cache_entries).

So `bin/docker-entrypoint`'s `./bin/rails db:prepare` sees the cache database already present (it is primary), finds zero migrations in a nonexistent migrations_paths, loads nothing, and reports success. The table is never created and the failure is silent at deploy time.

== SECONDARY PROBLEMS FOUND (filed separately) ==
1. Adaptive polling intervals are far too long even when everything works. 30 of 72 feeds sit at the 7-day MAX_POLL_INTERVAL; observed chosen intervals: 2.2h to 168h, median ~3-5 days. feed.rb:161 `ideal_seconds = 12.hours / posts_per_day` means a weekly feed polls every ~51h. Fresh will still look stale after the cache fix.
2. Thundering herd: 73 feeds enqueued per 5-min cycle against good_job.max_threads = 2, with a hard `sleep(1.5)` in UpdateFeedJob's ensure block plus up to 5s of DomainThrottler sleep. Floor is ~55s of pure sleep per cycle before any network I/O; it will not keep up once feeds actually fetch.
3. Race between the `last_update_started < 5.minutes.ago` guard and the */5 cron. The 22:10:00 run enqueued zero because it landed 4m58s after 22:05:02. Roughly every other cycle is randomly skipped.
4. config/deploy.yml sets SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA: true, but this app uses GoodJob, not Solid Queue. Inert leftover from the Rails 8 template, misleading when debugging job execution.

== FIX ORDER ==
prod: create solid_cache_entries (fix the database.yml url/database collision and the missing migrations_paths) -> UpdateFeedJob stops dying -> feeds fetch.
dev: start via `bin/dev`, not bare `rails server`.
Then revisit the polling interval math, which is the remaining reason Fresh lags.

title: Add guaranteed daily morning feed refresh cron that bypasses adaptive polling backoff
description:
Requested behavior: every morning, all feeds should already be refreshed before the app is opened, without any manual refresh click.

Current behavior: the only feed-refresh scheduler is `update_feeds` (config/initializers/good_job.rb:6), which runs every 5 minutes but only picks feeds whose `next_poll_at` is due under adaptive polling. Feeds that have been backed off to a long interval, or that are sitting behind `retry_after`, can stay stale indefinitely. There is no time-of-day guarantee.

Note the peer pattern already in the codebase: FetchStoriesJob is scheduled at fixed times (2am overnight, 2pm midday) and AnalyzeStoriesJob at 5am. A morning feed sweep would follow the same shape.

Proposed:
- Add a GoodJob cron entry (e.g. `refresh_all_feeds_morning`, around 5-6am local) that enqueues UpdateFeedJob for every active feed regardless of next_poll_at, while still respecting `retry_after` so rate-limited hosts are not hammered.
- Decide whether this is a new job class or a flag on UpdateFeedsJob (e.g. `UpdateFeedsJob.perform_later(force: true)`) that skips the adaptive_polling_condition.
- Confirm the app timezone so 'morning' means Andy's morning, not UTC.

Acceptance criteria:
- A cron entry exists that sweeps all active feeds once each morning.
- Rate-limit / retry_after protection is preserved (mirrors the guard in Api::V1::FeedsController#refresh, app/controllers/api/v1/feeds_controller.rb:58).
- Job test covers: backed-off feed IS picked up by the morning sweep; retry_after feed is NOT.

Blocked by ttrb-t9n0: no point adding another cron entry until we know why the existing cron is not firing.

Affected files:
- config/initializers/good_job.rb
- app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb
- test/jobs/
close_reason: Added UpdateFeedsJob force: flag and refresh_all_feeds_morning cron (6am America/New_York) that sweeps every feed past its adaptive polling window while preserving retry_after and concurrent-update guards. Commit f2784bf.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Context from ttrb-t9n0: adaptive polling currently pins 30 of 72 feeds at the 7-day MAX_POLL_INTERVAL, which is exactly the case a guaranteed daily refresh would paper over. See ttrb-u55y for fixing the interval math itself; decide whether both are wanted.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit f2784bf. Chose the flag over a new job class: force: keeps the retry_after and last_update_started guards in one place rather than duplicating them.

Implementation:
- UpdateFeedsJob#perform(force: false). feeds_to_update builds the guard scope first (retry_after IS NULL OR <= now; last_update_started IS NULL OR < 5.minutes.ago) and only appends adaptive_polling_condition when force is false. Both guards apply in force mode.
- config/initializers/good_job.rb: refresh_all_feeds_morning, cron "0 6 * * * America/New_York", kwargs: { force: true }.

Timezone: config.time_zone is commented out (config/application.rb:36) and deploy.yml sets no TZ, so the app runs UTC and every other cron entry is implicitly UTC despite comments reading like local time. Rather than change the app-wide zone, the entry carries an explicit zone field. GoodJob calls Fugit.parse(cron) (good_job-4.19.2 app/models/good_job/cron_entry.rb:187), and fugit parses the trailing zone: verified Fugit.parse gives next_time 2026-08-18 06:00:00 -0400. kwargs is likewise a real GoodJob feature, cron_entry.rb:134 does perform_later(*args_value, **kwargs_value).

Empirical check on dev's 72 feeds, inside a rolled-back transaction with all next_poll_at pushed to +7d and 3 feeds given retry_after +2h: normal mode 0 feeds, force mode 69. The 3 rate-limited feeds are the exact difference.

Tests: 5 new in test/jobs/update_feeds_job_test.rb (backed-off feed IS swept; retry_after feed is NOT; mid-update feed is NOT; expired retry_after IS; force takes all feeds regardless of next_poll_at) plus new test/config/good_job_cron_test.rb guarding the cron entry itself (registered, kwargs force: true, exactly one fire per day at 6am Eastern, and entry.enqueue actually enqueues UpdateFeedsJob with force: true). Full suite 367 runs 1012 assertions 0 failures; rubocop clean.

Note this does not fire in dev unless the app is started via bin/dev (execution_mode :external, per ttrb-t9n0).

title: Move production background jobs off :async in-Puma execution to a dedicated Kamal job host
description:
config/environments/production.rb:51 runs GoodJob with `execution_mode = :async` and `max_threads = 2`, meaning all background work (feed fetching, LLM story analysis, article caching, audio generation, digests) executes inside the Puma web process. config/deploy.yml:11-14 has the dedicated `job:` server block commented out:

    # job:
    #   hosts:
    #     - 192.168.1.208
    #   cmd: bin/jobs

Problems with async-in-web:
- In-flight jobs are lost on deploy/restart; long jobs (AnalyzeStoriesJob, GenerateArticleAudioJob) are the most exposed.
- Only 2 threads, competing with request-serving threads on the same process.
- If the web container is scaled to zero or idles, cron stops entirely, so scheduled refreshes silently stop.

Proposed: uncomment/enable the Kamal `job:` role running `bin/jobs` (the binstub already correctly boots `GoodJob::CLI`), switch production to `execution_mode = :external`, and keep `enable_cron = true` on the job role only so cron entries are not double-registered.

Acceptance criteria:
- Production runs a separate job process; web process no longer executes jobs.
- Cron entries fire exactly once per schedule (no duplicate enqueues from web + job roles).
- Verified after deploy that UpdateFeedsJob enqueues on schedule.

Related: ttrb-t9n0 (auto-refresh not working) may be caused by this.

Affected files:
- config/deploy.yml
- config/environments/production.rb

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Relevant data from ttrb-t9n0 diagnosis: production :async-in-Puma execution is in fact working, cron fires on schedule every 5 min. The blocker was never the execution mode. But max_threads=2 against 73 feeds per cycle with hard sleeps is a real capacity problem, see ttrb-771g.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 2553973: config change complete, deploy verification outstanding.

CHANGES
- config/environments/production.rb: execution_mode :async -> :external (max_threads/poll_interval/enable_cron unchanged).
- config/deploy.yml: uncommented the job role (hosts 192.168.1.208, cmd bin/jobs).
- config/deploy.yml: removed SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA: true. solid_queue is not in the Gemfile or Gemfile.lock and the var is referenced nowhere in the repo, so it was dead config that also misdescribed how jobs run.

WHY THIS GIVES EXACTLY-ONCE CRON (mechanism, verified in good_job 4.19.2 source)
- adapter.rb:277 start_async returns early unless execute_async?, and execute_async? (adapter.rb:256) is 'async_all || (async/async_server && in_webserver?)'. With :external it is false regardless of in_webserver?, so the Puma process starts no capsule.
- capsule.rb:48 builds the CronManager only inside capsule.start. No capsule in web means no cron and no job execution in web.
- cli.rb:118 calls capsule.start unconditionally, and configuration.enable_cron? is true, so bin/jobs is the sole cron registrant.

VERIFIED LOCALLY
- bin/kamal config -> roles [job, web]. Kamal::Configuration inspection: role=job proxy=false cmd="bin/jobs" container=nibbler-job; role=web proxy=true (unchanged).
- RAILS_ENV=production runner: execution_mode :external, execute_async? false, execute_externally? true, enable_cron? true, cron entries 8, max_threads 2.
- bundle exec rubocop config/environments/production.rb -> clean. bin/rails test -> 367 runs, 1012 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.

NOT VERIFIED (needs bin/kamal deploy, not run from this session)
- Third acceptance criterion: UpdateFeedsJob enqueues on schedule after deploy. Check with 'bin/kamal app logs -r job -f' on the */5 boundary. GoodJob.logger is Rails.logger (engine.rb:15) and production.rb logs to STDOUT, so job-role output reaches docker logs.
- Confirm the web role no longer logs job execution: 'bin/kamal app logs -r web' should show no Performing/Enqueued lines.
- Leaving this issue in_progress until that deploy check is done.

NOTES / FOLLOW-UPS
- max_threads is still 2, now on a dedicated process rather than shared with Puma. ttrb-771g (73 feeds per cycle vs 2 threads with hard sleeps) is untouched and still applies; the dedicated role removes request-thread contention but not the drain-time arithmetic.
- Deploy ordering: bin/docker-entrypoint only runs db:prepare when the command ends in './bin/rails server', so the job container starts without waiting for migrations. On a deploy that carries a migration the job process can briefly run against the old schema. Jobs retry, and this matches how the role would behave with any Kamal worker, so no change made.
- bin/jobs does not set GoodJob::CLI.within_exe = true (only the gem's own exe/good_job does). Harmless here: execution_mode is explicitly :external so the async->external coercion at configuration.rb:119 is never needed, and stdout logging already comes from production.rb. Setting it would be a defensive one-liner if execution_mode is ever changed back.

title: Remove vestigial config/queue.yml (Solid Queue config; project uses GoodJob)
description:
config/queue.yml contains Solid Queue worker/dispatcher configuration (polling_interval, batch_size, JOB_CONCURRENCY), but this project uses GoodJob:

- Gemfile:40 declares `gem "good_job"`
- `solid_queue` appears nowhere in Gemfile.lock
- config/environments/*.rb set `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :good_job`
- bin/jobs boots `GoodJob::CLI`

The file is leftover Rails 8 default scaffolding and is never read. It is actively misleading when debugging job execution, since it implies a JOB_CONCURRENCY / thread setting that has no effect (the real knobs are good_job.max_threads and good_job.poll_interval in config/environments/production.rb:52-53).

Acceptance criteria:
- config/queue.yml deleted.
- Grep confirms no reference to it (including bin/, config/deploy.yml, Dockerfile).
- App boots and jobs still run in dev and test.
close_reason: Deleted config/queue.yml (vestigial Solid Queue scaffolding). Dev boots with GoodJob, 63 job tests pass, bin/jobs loads.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 47ee8fc: deleted config/queue.yml. Verified no solid_queue reference anywhere in the tree, no queue database in config/database.yml, no db/queue_schema.rb, and nothing (bin/, config/deploy.yml, Dockerfile) reads the file. Dev boots with GoodJobAdapter and all 8 cron entries; 63 job tests pass (0 failures); bin/jobs help loads GoodJob::CLI.

title: Make Playwright E2E suite hermetic so it can run in PR CI
description:
CI now runs Minitest and Vitest (see .github/workflows/ci.yml), but the 213 Playwright specs are deliberately excluded, with the reasoning recorded as a comment at the bottom of that workflow.

Blockers to putting E2E in PR CI:
- Specs read and mutate live data (mark all read, star/unstar, create/delete labels and categories). db/seeds.rb creates only the admin user, no feeds or entries, so on a clean CI database roughly half the specs no-op through their test.skip data guards. A green run would not mean much.
- e2e/smoke.spec.ts 'refresh button triggers feed refresh' fetches real feed URLs over the public internet. Flaky and slow to put in front of every merge.
- Auto-auth depends on ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 plus a pre-existing user. ALLOW_DEV_AUTH is currently only set in test/test_helper.rb, not for a booted server.

Work needed:
- Fixture/seed path that creates deterministic feeds, entries, categories and labels for E2E.
- Stub or block external feed fetching during E2E.
- Boot the server for E2E with an explicit env (ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1) against a dedicated database.
- Then add the e2e job to .github/workflows/ci.yml and delete the explanatory comment block.
close_reason: E2E suite is hermetic (own server, own database, seeded fixture set, per-test reset, no external network) and runs as the test_e2e job in PR CI. 214 passed / 5 skipped locally, twice, identically.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit c7025cf: hermetic E2E suite landed.

New: bin/e2e-server (own server on 3001, own ttrb_e2e database, ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 / ALLOW_E2E_RESET=1 / OFFLINE_FEED_FETCH=1), lib/e2e_dataset.rb (deterministic fixture set), lib/tasks/e2e.rake, app/services/offline_feed_fetcher.rb, app/controllers/e2e_reset_controller.rb + gated POST /e2e/reset.

Changed: FeedFetcher.for is now the single place outbound feed fetches are built; playwright.config.ts starts bin/e2e-server with reuseExistingServer off and workers 1; e2e/fixtures/test.ts gained two auto fixtures (reset + sign in as seeded admin); test_e2e job added to .github/workflows/ci.yml and the explanatory comment block removed.

Three things blocked a green run beyond the four items in the description:
- ALLOW_DEV_AUTH does not cover Api::V1::SessionsController#show, so the UI always showed the login form. Filed ttrb-gwcr; the suite now logs in for real.
- FeedSidebar wiped its saved category expansion state on every load (effect pruned 'deleted' ids while categories was still empty), hiding every feed inside a folder. Fixed here; the unmet first-visit default is ttrb-qx8l.
- Much of the suite targeted /api/v1/labels with caption fields and numeric filter_type/action_type codes. Those APIs are /api/v1/tags with name, and string type names. Specs updated.
- smoke 'mark all read' asserted view=fresh returns zero afterwards, which the API never did. Now asserts unread=true. Fresh-view inconsistency filed as ttrb-y0na.

Data-availability test.skip guards replaced with assertions so a broken seed fails loudly.

Verified: 214 passed / 5 skipped (pre-existing deliberate skips) in 2.4m, twice with identical results. Minitest 367 runs 0 failures, Vitest 522 passed, rubocop 178 files 0 offenses.

title: Unmocked fetch in EntryContent and SettingsDialog vitest tests hits the real network
description:
Discovered while adding test jobs to CI (ttrb-3pyl).

'npm run test:run' prints unhandled ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000 errors. Bisected to two files:
- app/javascript/components/EntryContent.test.tsx
- app/javascript/components/SettingsDialog.test.tsx

Cause: API_BASE in app/javascript/lib/api.ts is the relative path '/api/v1'. happy-dom resolves relative URLs against its default base of http://localhost:3000, so a component that fires an unmocked fetch on mount attempts a real network request.

Today the suite still reports 27 files / 522 tests passing because the rejections land outside test context, and the same will hold in CI (connection refused fast, no server). But this is an unmocked boundary:
- It is a latent flake. If anything is listening on port 3000 on the machine running the tests, these tests exercise a live server instead of a stub.
- The rejection noise obscures real failures in the output.

Fix: mock the api module (or global fetch) at the boundary in both test files, per the project's 'mock at boundaries' guideline in docs/vitest-rtl-testing-guide.md.
close_reason: Mocked @/lib/api in EntryContent.test.tsx and SettingsDialog.test.tsx. Commit b614e78. Full suite 27 files / 522 tests passing with no ECONNREFUSED output.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit b614e78: mocked @/lib/api in EntryContent.test.tsx (api.entries.info via SuggestedTags, api.stories.extractFromEntry via FollowStoryDialog) and SettingsDialog.test.tsx (api.auth.publicFeedKey via AccountPanel, plus feeds/categories list). Full suite: 27 files / 522 tests passing, zero ECONNREFUSED output.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Filed ttrb-lf8q for a suite-wide global.fetch guard in test/setup.ts (verified it works and keeps the suite green, but it is silent rather than loud; test/setup.ts is outside this issue's scope).

title: Fix production solid_cache: cache DB resolves to primary and db/cache_migrate is missing, so solid_cache_entries never created
description:
Blocks all background feed refresh in production. Discovered while diagnosing ttrb-t9n0.

Every UpdateFeedJob dies at app/services/domain_throttler.rb:14 (Rails.cache.read) with:
  PG::UndefinedTable: relation "solid_cache_entries" does not exist

Two compounding config faults in config/database.yml production:
1. The cache: entry inherits 'url: ENV["DATABASE_URL"]' from &primary_production, which overrides its explicit 'database: nibbler_production_cache'. Verified both primary and cache resolve to database "nibbler_production".
2. migrations_paths: db/cache_migrate points at a directory that does not exist. Only db/cache_schema.rb exists (it defines solid_cache_entries).

Result: bin/docker-entrypoint's db:prepare sees the cache database already present (it is primary), finds zero migrations, creates nothing, and exits clean. Silent failure at deploy.

Fix options: give the cache config its own url (or drop the url inheritance and keep host/database), and either create db/cache_migrate or let db:prepare load db/cache_schema.rb. Verify after deploy that solid_cache_entries exists and that UpdateFeedJob completes past line 26.

Affected: config/database.yml, config/cache.yml, bin/docker-entrypoint, config/environments/production.rb:45
close_reason: Cache config given its own url derived from DATABASE_URL (+_cache), anchor inheritance dropped, db/cache_migrate created, regression test added. Verified end-to-end: db:prepare creates the cache db and loads solid_cache_entries; DomainThrottler round-trips. Needs a production deploy to take effect.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 72aa84d: cache entry no longer inherits the primary's url:. Root cause confirmed in Rails source (UrlConfig#initialize does configuration_hash.merge(build_url_hash), so url wins over database:) and empirically -- both entries resolved to nibbler_production before the fix, nibbler_production_cache after.

Silent-deploy-failure mechanism confirmed at DatabaseTasks#initialize_database:654: it gates schema loading on schema_migration.table_exists?, which was true because the cache pointed at the primary db, so db/cache_schema.rb was never loaded.

Verified end-to-end by running the real deploy command (RAILS_ENV=production ./bin/rails db:prepare, matching the Dockerfile CMD that bin/docker-entrypoint's guard matches on) against throwaway local databases: created nibbler_e2e_cache, loaded solid_cache_entries into it, second run idempotent, and DomainThrottler.record/wait_for (the app/services/domain_throttler.rb:14 failure site) round-tripped against a live SolidCache::Store. Scratch databases dropped afterward.

Also added db/cache_migrate/.keep (migrations_paths pointed at a nonexistent dir) and test/config/database_config_test.rb, which fails against the old config (asserted).

config/cache.yml needed no change; production 'database: cache' correctly selects the cache connection.

title: Make DomainThrottler degrade gracefully when the cache store is unavailable
description: DomainThrottler.wait_for (app/services/domain_throttler.rb:14) and .record (:29) call Rails.cache with no rescue. A broken cache store therefore takes down every UpdateFeedJob before it fetches anything (see ttrb-t9n0). Throttling is an optimization, not correctness: a cache failure should log and continue, not abort the feed update. Consider rescuing StandardError around the cache calls, or moving DomainThrottler.wait_for below the FeedUpdater call so a throttle failure cannot block the fetch.
close_reason: DomainThrottler.wait_for/.record now rescue StandardError around the cache calls, log a warning and continue unthrottled. 12 new tests in test/services/domain_throttler_test.rb. Full suite green (352 runs, 0 failures), rubocop clean.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit af3d352: rescued StandardError around the cache work in both DomainThrottler.wait_for and .record; failures log a warning (domain + error class/message) and the caller proceeds unthrottled. Kept wait_for above the FeedUpdater call -- the rescue makes the reorder unnecessary and FetchStoryArticlesJob has the same pattern, so fixing the throttler covers both callers.

Added test/services/domain_throttler_test.rb (12 tests): broken-store read/write, no-sleep-on-failure, corrupt cached value, plus healthy-path regression guards (records timestamp, sleeps the remaining delay, per-domain isolation, invalid URLs never touch the cache). Verified non-vacuous: 6 errors against the pre-fix service, 0 after.

Also grepped app/ and lib/ -- DomainThrottler was the only direct Rails.cache caller, so this closes the app-level exposure from ttrb-t9n0.

title: Adaptive polling intervals too long: 30 of 72 feeds pinned at the 7-day MAX_POLL_INTERVAL
description: Discovered while diagnosing ttrb-t9n0. Even with the scheduler working, Fresh will look stale. app/models/feed.rb:161 computes ideal_seconds = 12.hours / posts_per_day, i.e. poll only twice per expected post. A weekly feed gets a ~51h interval; a feed posting 3x/month gets 120h. Observed dev distribution of chosen intervals: 2.2h to 168h, with 30 of 72 feeds at the 168h MAX_POLL_INTERVAL cap and a median around 3-5 days. calculate_avg_posts_per_day also floors at 0.01 for feeds with no entries in the 30-day window, which maps straight to MAX_POLL_INTERVAL. Reconsider the multiplier and cap MAX_POLL_INTERVAL far below 7 days for feeds a user actually reads.
close_reason: Capped MAX_POLL_INTERVAL at 6h (was 7d) and raised polls-per-post to 4; added feeds:recalculate_poll_intervals to re-derive existing rows. Dev median interval 5d -> 6h.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 13a43cc. MAX_POLL_INTERVAL 7d -> 6h, polls per post 2 -> 4 (POLLS_PER_POST), 0.01 avg floor removed, Feed#recalculate_polling_interval! + rake feeds:recalculate_poll_intervals to re-derive existing rows. Verified in dev: before 31/72 at the 168h cap, median 5d, range 2.2h-168h; after 66/72 at the 6h cap, median 6h, range 66.7m-6h. Cost is ~336 conditional GETs/day for 72 feeds; FeedFetcher already sends If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since so a quiet feed returns 304 with no body. Full suite 358 runs 0 failures, rubocop clean. Filed ttrb-03h5 for the separate defect that avg_posts_per_day never decays for feeds that go quiet.

title: UpdateFeedJob thundering herd: 73 feeds per 5-min cycle against max_threads=2 with hard sleeps
description: Discovered while diagnosing ttrb-t9n0. Production enqueues 73 UpdateFeedJob per cron cycle into a GoodJob pool of max_threads=2 (config/environments/production.rb:43). Each job has an unconditional sleep(1.5) in its ensure block (app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb:42) plus up to 5s of DomainThrottler sleep. Floor is 73*1.5/2 = ~55s of pure sleep per cycle before any network I/O, and the sleeps burn worker threads rather than yielding. Once feeds actually fetch this will not drain within the 5-minute window. Consider a dedicated worker (config/deploy.yml job: block is commented out), more threads, or replacing the sleeps with scheduled_at spacing.
close_reason: Removed the unconditional sleep(1.5) from UpdateFeedJob and replaced DomainThrottler's blocking wait with scheduled_at rescheduling (new DomainThrottler.delay_for), so no job holds a worker thread while waiting. Sleep floor per cycle 55s+ -> 0. GoodJob max_threads 2 -> 5 (GOOD_JOB_MAX_THREADS) with database.yml max_connections derived to match. Dedicated job role was already in place from ttrb-k1qa. Added test/jobs/update_feed_job_test.rb (11 tests, job previously untested) plus 5 delay_for tests; suite 384 runs 0 failures, rubocop clean. Commit 3a654a8.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 3a654a8. Removed both sleeps from the hot path; the pool no longer loses threads to waiting.

WHAT CHANGED
1. app/jobs/update_feed_job.rb: INTER_REQUEST_DELAY (the unconditional sleep(1.5) in the ensure block) deleted. It was a global stand-in for a per-domain rate limit that DomainThrottler already enforces at the correct granularity; two feeds on unrelated hosts have no reason to be spaced apart.
2. app/services/domain_throttler.rb: added delay_for(url), returning the seconds still owed to a domain (0 = go now). wait_for is now a thin `sleep(delay_for(url))` wrapper, so its behaviour and its cache-failure rescue are unchanged. FetchStoryArticlesJob keeps wait_for deliberately: it loops over queries inside a single job and has nothing else to do with the thread.
3. UpdateFeedJob#defer_for_busy_domain: when delay_for is positive the job does `set(wait: delay).perform_later(feed.id, deferrals: n+1)` and returns, freeing the thread. Verified in good_job-4.19.2 that this does NOT cost a poll_interval (30s): adapter.rb:214-218 puts scheduled_at into the notified job_state and scheduler.rb:162-170 turns it into a delayed task, so an external worker wakes at the right moment via LISTEN/NOTIFY.
4. Deferral loop convergence: each pass lets exactly one feed on a domain through, so N same-domain feeds need N-1 deferrals. MAX_DEFERRALS = 5 bounds it; past the budget the job falls back to the (bounded, <=5s) blocking wait rather than rescheduling forever.
5. DomainThrottler.record moved into an ensure around the FeedUpdater call. A fetch that raised still hit the server, and retry_on would otherwise re-request it with zero domain delay. It stays out of the early-return paths (missing feed / mid-update / backoff / deferral), which never touch the network.
6. config/environments/production.rb: good_job.max_threads 2 -> ENV.fetch("GOOD_JOB_MAX_THREADS", 5). The same pool runs AnalyzeStoriesJob against Ollama; one slow analyze job on a 2-thread pool halves feed throughput.
7. config/database.yml: max_connections is now max(RAILS_MAX_THREADS, GOOD_JOB_MAX_THREADS + 2), covering whichever role boots the file. The +2 is GoodJob::SharedExecutor::MAX_THREADS, which is what GoodJob::Configuration.total_estimated_threads counts when it warns about pool undersizing. Verified by resolving the real config: no env -> 7, RAILS_MAX_THREADS=12 -> 12, GOOD_JOB_MAX_THREADS=10 -> 12.

NOT DONE HERE
The dedicated-worker option named in this issue is already in place: the deploy.yml `job:` block was uncommented in 2553973 (ttrb-k1qa), so execution_mode is :external and jobs no longer run inside Puma. No deploy.yml change was needed.

BUDGET AFTER THE FIX
Sleep floor per cycle drops from ~55s (plus up to ~180s of throttle sleep) to 0. Remaining per-cycle cost is real network I/O only: 73 feeds at ~1.5s each over 5 threads is ~22s, well inside the 5-minute window. The steady-state load is much lighter anyway now that ttrb-u55y capped intervals at 6h; the 73-feed burst is the morning force sweep.

TESTS
New test/jobs/update_feed_job_test.rb (11 tests) - the job had none. Covers: no sleep on the free-domain path, no sleep on the defer path, defers instead of fetching when the domain is busy, reschedules at the right offset with deferrals incremented, fetches without rescheduling once the budget is spent, records the request time, records it even when the fetch raises, and the three pre-existing guards (missing feed, mid-update, backoff). The test env uses :null_store, which can never report a busy domain, so the tests swap in a MemoryStore.

Verified the no-sleep guards are non-vacuous: temporarily restored `ensure sleep(1.5)` and got 3 failures, removed it and got 11/11.

test/services/domain_throttler_test.rb +5 tests for delay_for. Two existing assertions updated: the cache-failure warning now reads "DomainThrottler#delay_for skipped ..." because that is genuinely where the read happens.

Full suite 384 runs, 1045 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. rubocop clean across 179 files.

title: UpdateFeedsJob 5-min guard races the */5 cron and randomly skips cycles
description: Discovered while diagnosing ttrb-t9n0. app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb:18 filters on last_update_started < 5.minutes.ago while the cron runs every 5 minutes, so whether a feed qualifies depends on a few seconds of jitter. Observed in production: the 22:10:00 run enqueued zero feeds because it landed 4m58s after the 22:05:02 run, while 21:50/21:55/22:00/22:05 each enqueued 73. Roughly every other cycle is silently skipped. Use a guard window shorter than the cron period, or key the guard off next_poll_at alone.

title: Feed#update_polling_stats! never lowers avg_posts_per_day for feeds that go quiet
description: app/models/feed.rb:114 only recalculates avg_posts_per_day when new_entries_count > 0, so the '30-day rolling average' never rolls down. A feed that used to post 5x/day and then stops keeps avg_posts_per_day 5.0 indefinitely and is polled every ~1.2h forever. The error is in the safe direction (over-polling, not staleness) and is bounded by MIN_POLL_INTERVAL, which is why it is low priority. Fix is to recalculate on every successful poll, or to recalculate when last_new_entry_at is older than ROLLING_AVERAGE_DAYS. Discovered while working on ttrb-u55y.

Tests added for decay to zero, decay toward the true windowed rate, and interval derived from the window (60 entries -> 2/day -> 3h). Full suite green: 398 runs, 0 failures.

title: Add .kamal/secrets to .gitignore - production credentials are currently committable
description:
`.kamal/secrets` exists in the working tree, is untracked, and is NOT matched by any .gitignore rule (`git check-ignore -v .kamal/secrets` finds no match). It contains 3 literal KEY=value lines.

config/deploy.yml declares SECRET_KEY_BASE, DATABASE_URL and POSTGRES_PASSWORD as secrets, so this file holds production credentials. Any `git add -A` / `git commit -a` commits them, and once pushed they are in history permanently.

Kamal's generated .gitignore normally carries `.kamal/secrets*`; this repo is missing it.

Fix: add `.kamal/secrets*` to .gitignore. Verify with `git check-ignore -v .kamal/secrets`.

Also confirm the file was never committed: `git log --all --oneline -- .kamal/secrets`. If it was, the credentials need rotating, not just ignoring.

Discovered while verifying deploy config during ttrb-3byu.
close_reason: Added .kamal/secrets* to .gitignore (bc8f2ff); verified with git check-ignore. No credential rotation needed, history was clean.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Verified by shape inspection (values not printed):

Current untracked .kamal/secrets holds three LITERAL credentials:
  SECRET_KEY_BASE   literal, 128 chars
  DATABASE_URL      literal, 78 chars (embeds the password)
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD literal, 24 chars

Git history is clean, so NO rotation is needed. The file was tracked in c88937f and 14a6503 and deleted from tracking in 4c9caec, but both committed versions were templates: c88937f used the stock Kamal \$(cat config/master.key) command substitution, 14a6503 sourced .kamal/secrets.env. No raw credential was ever committed.

So the exposure is prospective only: the file is untracked AND unignored, so a single 'git add -A' commits live production credentials. Fix is just the .gitignore entry.

title: .dockerignore misses .uv-cache/.venv/tags - production image is 10.8GB instead of ~600MB
description:
Built the production image to verify the new Gemfile.lock (ttrb-3byu) and it came out at 10.8GB.

Measured inside the image:
  /rails                    7.9G
  /rails/.uv-cache          7.6G   <- Python uv cache: PyTorch (1.4G x2) + nvidia/cudnn (988M)
  /rails/tags               129M   <- ctags index
  /rails/lib                 66M
  /rails/.venv               59M
plus coverage/, playwright-report/, e2e/, test/, docs/, .beads/, .claude/, .playwright-mcp/

Cause: Docker does NOT read .gitignore. These paths are all correctly gitignored (verified with git check-ignore) and none are tracked, but .dockerignore has no entry for them, so 'COPY . .' in the build stage pulls them in. Local sizes: .uv-cache 9.1G, tags 630M, .venv 57M.

Impact: every 'kamal deploy' builds and pushes a ~10.8GB image to the registry at 192.168.1.208:5555 instead of roughly 600MB. Slow deploys, wasted registry and host disk.

Fix: add to .dockerignore
  /.uv-cache
  /.venv
  /tags
  /coverage
  /playwright-report
  /e2e
  /test
  /docs
  /.beads
  /.claude
  /.playwright-mcp

Verify by rebuilding and checking 'docker images' size drops to the hundreds of MB.

Note the existing .dockerignore covers /node_modules/, /log/*, /tmp/*, /storage/*, /public/assets and /.git, so this is a gap rather than a missing file.

Discovered while verifying the dependency re-resolve in ttrb-3byu.
close_reason: Added the missing .dockerignore entries. Production image 10.8GB -> 484MB, build context ~10G -> 69MB, verified by rebuild; image still boots Rails in production.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit b032619: added the missing entries to .dockerignore.

Verified empirically:
- Build context: ~10G -> 69MB (measured with a busybox COPY . probe)
- Final image: 10.8GB -> 484MB (docker images), /rails 7.9G -> 170M
- All 11 listed paths confirmed absent from /rails in the built image
- Image still boots: 'bin/rails runner' in production prints Rails 8.1.3.1, 85 routes, asset manifest present, TtsGenerator autoloads

Two corrections to the original report:
1. .venv is not 57M, it is 6.8G. It hardlinks its site-packages into .uv-cache, so 'du' on both paths at once attributes the shared inodes to whichever is listed first. Same accounting explains the 7.6G/59M split measured inside the image.
2. Only .uv-cache, .venv, tags, coverage, playwright-report and .playwright-mcp are gitignored. test/, e2e/, docs/, .beads/ and .claude/ are tracked files, so they were shipping deliberately rather than through a gitignore/dockerignore mismatch. Excluded them anyway - a production image has no use for them.

Also added /uv.lock, /test-results, /.lsp.json and /.mcp.json while in the file.

Remaining weight in the 484MB image: /rails/tmp 94M (bootsnap cache, wanted) and /rails/lib 66M (TTS .onnx voice models, dead weight - see ttrb-h45v).

title: TTS is non-functional in the production image - .venv python symlink is host-absolute and final stage has no Python
description:
Discovered while fixing ttrb-ad1w (.dockerignore gap).

app/services/tts_generator.rb:14 runs Rails.root.join('.venv','bin','python3'). In the repo, .venv/bin/python3 -> python -> /bin/python3.12, an absolute symlink to the host interpreter, and .venv/pyvenv.cfg has home = /bin.

The Dockerfile installs python-is-python3 only in the throw-away build stage. The final stage is plain ruby:3.4.7-slim with no Python at all, so /bin/python3.12 does not exist there. Even before ttrb-ad1w excluded .venv from the build context, the venv that shipped in the image was a dangling symlink pointing at a nonexistent interpreter, so GenerateArticleAudioJob / TtsGenerator could only ever return 'Python TTS script failed'.

Two follow-ups:
1. Decide whether TTS should work in production. If yes, the venv has to be built inside the image (install python3 + uv in the final stage, or a dedicated stage that produces a relocatable venv) rather than copied from the host. If no, gate TtsGenerator behind a config flag so the API returns a clear 'unavailable' rather than a subprocess error.
2. lib/tts/models/*.onnx is 61M and is still copied into the image (it is gitignored but lib/ as a whole is needed for bootsnap precompile). Those voice models are dead weight while TTS cannot run - they are the single largest remaining item in the ~69M build context. Either exclude them or make them part of a working TTS image.
close_reason: Gated TTS behind TtsGenerator.available? (TTS_ENABLED / venv detection), API now returns status unavailable instead of a subprocess error, and dropped the 61M voice models from the build context. Decided against building the venv into the image.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit eba2197: TtsGenerator.available? gates on config.x.tts.enabled (TTS_ENABLED) or the venv interpreter actually resolving; /audio returns status "unavailable" and skips the job; React handles the terminal status in useTtsPlayer and AudioPlayerContext. .dockerignore drops lib/tts/models and **/__pycache__ - scratch COPY-everything probe measured 65.6MB -> 2.4MB context, lib/*.rb and generate.py still present for bootsnap. Decision on follow-up 1: TTS stays out of the production image; the venv is 6.8G because forcealign pulls torch + CUDA. Filed ttrb-rvm4 for the pre-existing AudioPlayerContext gap on server status "error".

title: Space in article view should page down through content, then advance to next article at the end
description:
Desired behavior: while reading an article, pressing Space pages down through the article body. When already at the bottom of the content, the next Space advances to the next article (scrolled to the top). So holding a reading rhythm on one key: page, page, page, next article, page, page...

Current behavior: Space is bound directly to `handleKeyboardNextUnread` (application.tsx:725, `{ key: " ", handler: handleKeyboardNextUnread, description: "Next unread" }`). It always jumps to the next unread entry immediately, with no paging. Paging exists but is on a separate, less reachable binding: Ctrl+F / Ctrl+B -> `handleContentPageDown` / `handleContentPageUp` (application.tsx:685-701), which scrollBy `clientHeight * 0.9` on `contentScrollRef`.

Implementation sketch:
- New handler (e.g. `handleSpacePageOrAdvance`) replacing the Space binding. Reads `contentScrollRef.current`; if `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight - threshold`, page down; otherwise delegate to the existing next-entry handler.
- Reuse `handleContentPageDown`'s 0.9 * clientHeight overlap so a line or two of context carries over between pages.
- Reset scroll to top when the new article renders (confirm whether the content pane already does this on entry change).
- Bind Shift+Space to page up / previous article as the mirror. The KeyboardCommand type already supports `modifiers: { shift: true }` and `matchesModifiers` requires an exact match, so Space and Shift+Space can coexist as separate entries.

Traps to handle:
- `scrollBy` uses `behavior: "smooth"`. If the bottom check reads live `scrollTop` while a smooth scroll is still animating, rapid Space presses will misread position and skip to the next article early. Track the intended target offset, or use a settled/instant scroll for this path.
- Iframe view (toggled with `i`) renders third-party content, where scroll position is not measurable cross-origin. Decide the fallback: probably keep the old advance-immediately behavior when in iframe mode.
- Space must keep its existing no-op inside inputs; `isInputElement` in hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts already guards this, but verify Space in a search box or comment field still types a space rather than paging.
- Space currently means 'next UNREAD' specifically, not 'next entry'. Confirm which one the advance step should use, since j/n use `handleKeyboardNext`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Space pages down within a long article without changing entries.
- Space at the bottom of the content advances to the next article, and the new article starts at the top.
- Space on a short article that fits entirely on screen advances immediately (no dead keypress).
- Shift+Space mirrors the behavior upward.
- KeyboardShortcutsDialog is updated to describe the new Space behavior.
- Vitest coverage for: page-down case, at-bottom advance case, short-article immediate advance, and Space inside an input.

Affected files:
- app/javascript/application.tsx (keyboardCommands list, handlers around lines 685-748)
- app/javascript/hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts (if the matching logic needs changes)
- app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx
close_reason: Space now pages down through the article body and advances to the next unread entry only at the end; Shift+Space mirrors upward. Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B share the same paging state. Iframe view keeps immediate advance. Vitest coverage added in useContentPaging.test.ts.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit ba6e7d6: new useContentPaging hook drives Space (page down, then next unread) and Shift+Space (page up, then previous entry); Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B now route through the same hook so both paths share pending-scroll state. Smooth-scroll race handled by paging from the pending target instead of live scrollTop. Iframe view falls through to immediate navigation. EntryContent resets the viewport to the top on entry change. 21 new tests in useContentPaging.test.ts plus a Space-inside-input test in useKeyboardCommands.test.ts; full vitest suite 544 passed.

title: Decide tracking policy for public/icons/ favicon cache (currently 63 untracked files)
description:
Request: commit the untracked public/icons/ directory (63 files, ~967 KB: 28 .ico, 28 .png, 5 .jpg, 2 .svg).

IMPORTANT - read before committing. Evidence says these are a regenerable runtime cache, not source assets:

- app/jobs/fetch_favicon_job.rb writes them. Filenames are `"#{feed.id}#{extension}"` (fetch_favicon_job.rb:32-33), so every name is keyed to a local database primary key. On any other database those IDs point at different feeds, making the committed files wrong rather than merely stale.
- The directory is created on demand via `FileUtils.mkdir_p(ICONS_DIR)` (fetch_favicon_job.rb:52-54), so nothing breaks if it is absent from a fresh checkout.
- UpdateFaviconsJob runs daily at 4am (config/initializers/good_job.rb:16) and rewrites these files, so tracking them produces a permanent stream of modified-binary noise in git status and bloats history with churned binaries.
- The directly analogous cache, /public/audio/cache/, is already gitignored (.gitignore:54), as is /public/assets (.gitignore:31). public/icons/ looks like an oversight in the same list.

Two options:

A. Gitignore it (recommended). Add `/public/icons/` to .gitignore. Favicons repopulate automatically on the next UpdateFaviconsJob run, or immediately via FetchFaviconJob per feed. Confirm the production deploy does not depend on the directory being present in the image at boot (it should not, given mkdir_p), and confirm nothing in config/deploy.yml expects a baked-in icons dir rather than a persistent volume.

B. Commit them as requested. Only makes sense if these should ship as seeded/default icons for a fresh install. If so they should probably not live under a job-writable path at all, since UpdateFaviconsJob will overwrite them; move seeds elsewhere and have the job write to a separate cache dir.

Note: if B is chosen, production also needs a persistent volume or the cache is lost on every container restart, which is a separate concern worth checking either way.

Acceptance criteria:
- A decision recorded on this issue.
- Either .gitignore updated (A) or the files committed with the seed/cache split resolved (B).
- `git status` clean with respect to public/icons after the change.
close_reason: Option A chosen: /public/icons/ gitignored as a regenerable cache (commit 4640ded). Files are keyed to local Feed primary keys and rewritten daily by UpdateFaviconsJob, so they are not seed assets. Filed ttrb-t2eq and ttrb-4pk6 for two production favicon bugs found while verifying.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
DECISION: Option A (gitignore). All four evidence points in the description verified independently:

1. fetch_favicon_job.rb:33 names files by local Feed primary key. Production runs a separate postgres DB (deploy.yml accessories.db), so committed files would be actively wrong there, not merely stale.
2. mkdir_p at fetch_favicon_job.rb:52-54 confirmed; nothing breaks on a fresh checkout.
3. UpdateFaviconsJob runs daily at 4am (good_job.rb update_favicons) and rewrites these files.
4. /public/audio/cache/ (.gitignore:54) and /public/assets (.gitignore:31) are the analogous already-ignored caches.

Additional verification the description asked for:
- ICONS_DIR / public/icons appears in exactly one file repo-wide (fetch_favicon_job.rb). No frontend, seed, fixture, or test references it. Serving is driven by Feed#icon_url from the DB, not by a directory listing.
- config/deploy.yml has no expectation of a baked-in icons dir. No volumes: key; asset_path bridges /rails/public/assets only.
- The files were never tracked (git log --all and git ls-files on public/icons are both empty), so no history rewrite was needed.

Option B rejected: these are not seed assets. They are one user's dev-database cache, and UpdateFaviconsJob would overwrite them anyway.

Two production bugs found while verifying, filed separately:
- ttrb-t2eq: Dockerfile:58 is COPY . . and .dockerignore does not exclude /public/icons, so this dev cache is currently baked into production images and serves wrong icons on ID collision. One-line fix, left out of this issue's scope since .dockerignore was not in the stated scope.
- ttrb-4pk6: cache is ephemeral in production and UpdateFaviconsJob keys off favicon_last_checked rather than file existence, so favicons 404 for up to 7 days after each deploy.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 4640ded: added /public/icons/ to .gitignore with an explanatory comment. git status is now clean with respect to public/icons; git check-ignore confirms both the directory and its contents match .gitignore:60. No Ruby or JS changed, so no test run was warranted.

title: Fresh view is inconsistent: /api/v1/entries filters by date only, /api/v1/counters counts unread+recent
description:
The Fresh virtual folder means two different things depending on which endpoint you ask.

Api::V1::CountersController#index computes virtual.fresh as current_user.user_entries.unread.joins(:entry).where('entries.date_entered > ?', 24.hours.ago) - unread AND recent.

Api::V1::EntriesController#index (view=fresh) applies only where('entries.updated > ?', cutoff); there is no unread filter. #headlines does the same. The frontend (app/javascript/application.tsx around line 200) does not add unread=true for the fresh view either, it only passes fresh_max_age/fresh_per_feed.

So the sidebar badge counts unread recent articles while clicking Fresh lists every recent article including ones already read. The two also disagree on which column they filter: date_entered (counters) vs updated (entries).

Found while making the Playwright suite hermetic: e2e/smoke.spec.ts 'mark all read works' asserted view=fresh returned zero entries afterwards, which the API never did. That spec now queries unread=true instead.

Decide which reading is correct and make counters, entries#index and entries#headlines agree.
close_reason: Fresh is now unread + published within the window across counters, entries#index and entries#headlines; single UserEntry.fresh scope plus shared FreshArticleWindow concern. Commit 200950a.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 200950a: Fresh is now unread + entries.updated within the window everywhere. UserEntry.fresh(cutoff) is the single definition; FreshArticleWindow concern resolves the window for both controllers; counters accepts fresh_max_age and the frontend passes the view's age selector so the badge matches the list. Also fixed a pre-existing 500 in entries#headlines (bare .count over a multi-column select produced invalid COUNT(...) SQL) - it had to work before the agreement test could exercise it.

title: ALLOW_DEV_AUTH does not cover Api::V1::SessionsController, so dev auth alone never renders the reader
description:
Api::V1::BaseController#require_auth falls back to User.first when ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1. Api::V1::SessionsController does not inherit from BaseController and defines its own require_auth with no such fallback, so GET /api/v1/auth/me returns 401 even with the flag set.

The React app calls /api/v1/auth/me on boot to decide between LoginPage and the reader, so a browser with ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 and no session cookie sees the login form while every /api/v1 data endpoint would happily answer. The flag looks enabled but does nothing for anyone driving the UI.

Found while making the Playwright suite hermetic; the E2E fixtures now log in for real (POST /api/v1/auth/login as the seeded admin) rather than relying on the fallback.

Either extend the fallback to sessions#show or drop ALLOW_DEV_AUTH, but the two halves should not disagree.
close_reason: Removed ALLOW_DEV_AUTH; SessionsController inherits BaseController so /api/v1 auth is uniform. Tests sign in for real; added the missing sessions controller test.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit c2d6442: dropped ALLOW_DEV_AUTH entirely rather than extending the fallback.

Api::V1::SessionsController now inherits from BaseController and skips require_auth only for #create, so the two halves cannot disagree again; BaseController#require_auth just 401s. The flag is gone from bin/e2e-server, bin/dev and docs/playwright-testing-guide.md.

Chose removal over extension for two reasons: nothing needs it now that the E2E fixtures log in for real, and an env var that authenticates any request as User.first is a footgun one misconfigured deploy away from account takeover (see ttrb-iob, which gated the same bypass behind this flag in January).

Test-side fallout: the six /api/v1 controller tests got their session from the fallback. They now call sign_in(User.first) in setup. test_helper.rb's sign_in posted to /session, which is not a route, and sign_in_as was an empty stub with a comment admitting it did nothing; replaced with one helper that POSTs to /api/v1/auth/login and asserts the response.

Added test/controllers/api/v1/sessions_controller_test.rb (14 tests) - the controller had none. Includes a regression test asserting /api/v1/auth/me and /api/v1/feeds return identical 401 bodies for an anonymous request.

E2E: the 'Protected routes' block asserted ok() on endpoints its own test names said required authentication. Now parameterised over four paths, checking both the signed-in and the logged-out response.

Verified: Minitest 432 runs / 1280 assertions / 0 failures (was 418/1159), Vitest 550 passed, Playwright 219 passed / 5 skipped, rubocop 184 files / 0 offenses, tsc clean.

title: FeedSidebar does not default new users to expanded categories despite the comment saying it does
description:
app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx initialises expandedCategories from localStorage and falls back to new Set(categories.map(c => c.id)). At mount the categories prop is still empty (the request has not returned), so a browser with no saved state gets an empty set and every folder renders collapsed, hiding all feeds. The comment above it says 'defaulting to all expanded'.

A related defect in the same effect - it wiped the saved set on every load because the stale-id cleanup ran against the empty categories list - was fixed while making the Playwright suite hermetic (guarded with an early return when categories.length === 0). That restored persistence but not the intended first-visit default.

Fix: on the first run with real categories, expand all of them when localStorage had no saved entry (distinguish 'nothing saved' from 'saved an empty set').

title: Add a global unmocked-fetch guard to test/setup.ts
close_reason: globalThis.fetch guard added to test/setup.ts: records, logs, and throws on an unmocked call, and the existing afterEach fails the test on any recorded URL. Verified against a listener on port 3000 that the request no longer leaves the process. Commit cdc4e92.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit cdc4e92: guard in test/setup.ts replaces globalThis.fetch (global.fetch does not typecheck under this tsconfig). Resolves the silence caveat three ways: records the URL, console.errors it, and throws; the existing afterEach then fails the test on any recorded URL, after cleanup() so DOM teardown still runs. Verified with a TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:3000 and a throwaway test that swallows the rejection: guard off, the listener logs 'GET /api/v1/feeds HTTP/1.1 ... HappyDOM/20.11.2' and the test passes green; guard on, zero connections and the test fails with the URL named. Full suite 28 files / 550 tests before and after, tsc --noEmit clean. Also documented under Mocking Patterns in docs/vitest-rtl-testing-guide.md.

title: next_poll_at intervals that are multiples of 5 min always slip a full cron cycle
description:
Discovered while fixing ttrb-q19b (same class of bug, different guard).

UpdateFeedsJob runs on */5 and selects feeds with next_poll_at <= Time.current. Feed#update_polling_stats! sets next_poll_at = Time.current + interval, where Time.current is the moment the poll *completed*, always a few seconds after the cron tick that scheduled it. Any interval that is a multiple of the 5-minute cron period therefore lands just past the matching tick and waits a whole extra cycle.

Concretely: a feed at Feed::MIN_POLL_INTERVAL (5 min) polled at 22:05:07 gets next_poll_at 22:10:07; the 22:10:02 run skips it and it polls at 22:15, an effective 10-minute interval. Feed::DEFAULT_NEW_FEED_INTERVAL (15 min) becomes 20, and any manual update_interval of 5/10/15/30 minutes is similarly inflated by 5.

Options: select with a small lookahead (next_poll_at <= Time.current + 30.seconds), or subtract slack when computing next_poll_at. Either way the fix belongs in one place so the scheduler and the interval math agree.
close_reason: Scheduler looks Feed::POLL_DUE_SLACK (1 min) ahead of the cron tick, so intervals that are multiples of the 5-minute period no longer wait an extra cycle. Commit 55c5757.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 55c5757: scheduler now compares against Time.current + Feed::POLL_DUE_SLACK (1 min) instead of Time.current. Chose the lookahead over subtracting slack in update_polling_stats! so it also covers the legacy last_updated branch and feeds whose next_poll_at was written by the old code. retry_after deliberately left on the real clock. Tests: 3 new regression tests in test/jobs/update_feeds_job_test.rb (adaptive tick, legacy tick, slack bounds); verified they fail with POLL_DUE_SLACK = 0. Full suite 438 runs, 0 failures.

title: AudioPlayerContext#requestTtsAudio ignores server status "error", leaving the panel stuck in loading
description:
app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx requestTtsAudio branches on "generating" and "ready" only. When GET /api/v1/entries/:id/audio replies status "error" (a previously failed GenerateArticleAudioJob), no branch matches, so state stays "loading" and the audio panel spins forever with no message.

useTtsPlayer.ts handles the same response correctly (sets state "error" plus the message); the context is the copy that drifted. Pre-existing; found while adding the "unavailable" status in ttrb-h45v, which had to be handled in both places for the same reason.

Also in that file: the queue pre-generate poll (pollForReady) retries forever on any non-ready status, so a terminal error keeps a setTimeout chain alive for the life of the page.
close_reason: requestTtsAudio and both queue pre-generate polls now treat "error"/"unavailable" as terminal (commit 4601c94); tests added. Follow-ups filed: ttrb-2rmb, ttrb-8txz, ttrb-q7o3.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 4601c94: added isTerminalAudioStatus/terminalAudioMessage helpers; requestTtsAudio now handles "error" on both the initial response and the generating poll (poll interval is cleared), and both queue pre-generate polls (pollForAudio, pollForReady) stop on a terminal status instead of retrying forever. New app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.test.tsx covers all four paths; verified the 3 error-path tests fail against the pre-fix branch logic. Full suite 554 passed, tsc clean.

title: KeyboardShortcutsDialog documents 'k / p' as Previous entry but p toggles published
description: In app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx the Navigation section lists 'k / p' => 'Previous entry', but application.tsx binds p to handleKeyboardTogglePublished (key 'p' in the Actions group) and only k is previous entry. The dialog should list 'k' for previous entry and 'p' for toggle published. Found while updating the dialog for ttrb-gi13.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
